2025-09.daily_overview: Today saw important progress in financial management. In the morning, after sorting out the details of the family's idle funds, I called the bank account manager Li Guodong during the lunch break to consult about wealth management products and received a specific, prudent plan. In the evening, I had a rational discussion with my husband Zhang Weiming, and we finally reached a consensus on investing in a combination of structured deposits and short-duration bond funds, shifting the family's financial management approach toward prudent allocation. For dinner, because my husband's new dish failed, we ordered takeout as a temporary measure, slightly breaking our usual routine.

events.name: Organize a breakdown of idle funds
events.description: On the morning of September 25, 2025, Yu Xiaowei opened her personal computer in the study, exported the past six months of income and expense records from online banking, and manually checked receipts for large expenditures. She calculated that she had about HK$300,000 that could be flexibly used, spread across savings and current accounts. In red ink, she wrote down the current deposit interest rates and the history of not taking any investment action, then closed the folder and put it into her handbag, planning to contact the bank during her lunch break.

events.name: Called Li Guodong during lunch break to consult about wealth management
events.description: During the lunch break on September 25, 2025, at about 12:30, Yu Xiaowei walked with her phone and notebook to the outdoor platform of the AIA Building and called Li Guodong, Senior Manager of HSBC's Wealth Management Department. She explained why she was calling, and Li Guodong quickly offered suggestions: a short-term bond fund with an annualized return of 3.2% and good liquidity; and a two-year principal-protected structured deposit with expected returns linked to exchange rates but guaranteed principal. Yu Xiaowei repeated the key points and jotted them down quickly: risk level, minimum investment of 50,000 Hong Kong dollars, redemption rules, and so on. Li Guodong reminded her that the bank's internal systems would be under maintenance during the National Day holiday, and suggested she sign the contract at the Central Branch on the first working day after the holiday, October 8. The call lasted about 25 minutes. Yu Xiaowei returned to her desk and transcribed the notes into the dedicated family finance notebook.

events.name: Husband's failed attempt at a new dish and takeout dinner
events.description: In the evening, Zhang Weiming wanted to try making a low-fat baked rice with mushrooms and chicken breast, but because he didn't control the heat well, the surface was burnt black while the inside was still undercooked. Yu Xiaowei saw the messy kitchen and couldn't help complaining a few words, but then calmed down. After discussing, they ordered a healthy salad takeout. Although it was close to the end of the fasting window, she only ate the vegetables and chicken breast, skipping the staple food, and tried to stay within her fasting principles.

events.name: Discussed with her husband and finalized the investment portfolio.
events.description: At around 8 pm on September 25, 2025, after Yu Xiaowei had calmed down a little, the two sat down on the living room sofa. She spread out the materials and explained the differences between the two products. Zhang Weiming listened and stroked his chin: “It’s better to play it safe; put the bulk of the money in deposits.” But Yu Xiaowei, considering that the family might need flexible funds to handle emergencies, leaned toward maintaining liquidity. After about 30 minutes of discussion, the two decided to buy 200,000 Hong Kong dollars of structured deposits and put 100,000 Hong Kong dollars into a short-term bond fund. Yu Xiaowei drew a pie chart in her notebook and marked the proportions, smiling: “This way we have both a ballast stone and liquid funds.” They agreed to go to Central together on October 8 to sign the contract.

start_state.mood: Focused and sharp

end_state.location: Living room at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District
end_state.mood: Feeling at ease, with a stronger sense of teamwork as a couple

events.name: Confirm the financial plan and appointment for signing
events.description: At about 10 a.m. on September 26, 2025, Yu Xiaowei called Li Guodong again from her workstation at AIA and clearly conveyed the investment plan agreed with her husband: a HK$100,000 short-term bond fund and a HK$200,000 principal-guaranteed structured deposit. After Li Guodong wrote it down, both parties confirmed they would meet at 2 p.m. on October 8 in the private meeting room at HSBC Central Branch, bringing their ID card, bank card, and proof of address, among other documents. After hanging up, Yu Xiaowei created a reminder event in her phone calendar and saved a screenshot of the document checklist.

events.name: Unexpected call from a Shenzhen client
events.description: During the lunch break, client Wang Qiming suddenly called, saying he wanted to purchase high-end medical insurance for two newly added executives at the Shenzhen branch and hoped to finalize the plan before National Day. Yu Xiaowei had to give up her break, and in the pantry, while eating a sandwich, she used her laptop to retrieve documents and discussed policy details with Wang Qiming for 30 minutes. They agreed to send the formal proposal after the holiday. Although it disrupted her midday study plan, she felt it was worth it to have secured another piece of business.

events.name: Q3 performance review and effectiveness evaluation
events.description: On the afternoon of September 26, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and Su Lishan walked into the meeting room with laptops. They exported each member's policy signing count, customer feedback, and satisfaction scores for the third quarter from the system and generated comparison charts, focusing on the changes in indicators since the reforms at the beginning of September. The data showed that overall policy signings increased by 8% month over month, customer satisfaction improved slightly, and new employee Li Ming had become noticeably more motivated under mentoring responsibilities. Although some senior employees had not fully adapted to job rotation, the division of labor adjustments had initially improved team collaboration efficiency. Yu Xiaowei used a highlighter to mark key turning points while Su Lishan took notes, providing a basis for the fourth-quarter plan.

2025-09.daily_overview: On Saturday, she stayed in seclusion all day to prepare for the exam, strictly following the real exam schedule to take a mock test for the CFP investment planning module. In the afternoon, she self-graded and analyzed her mistakes; in the evening, she compiled a topic-specific intensive review list and made a detailed study plan for October, officially launching the final sprint phase. Before bed, she used a massage gun to relieve stiffness in her lower body from prolonged sitting.

events.name: High-fidelity mock exam
events.description: On Saturday morning at 8:30, Yu Xiaowei cleared her desk in her home study, leaving only a pen, scratch paper, and a glass of plain water. She opened the official CFP online mock exam system and, strictly following the real exam timing, completed all 160 practice questions in the investment planning module within 3 hours with full concentration. Several times she frowned and bit her pen, especially pausing for a long time and repeatedly recalculating when encountering complex calculations involving estate trusts. After submitting her paper at 11:30 noon, she finally breathed a sigh of relief.

events.name: Grading and in-depth review
events.description: After a simple bowl of wonton noodles at one o'clock in the afternoon, Yu Xiaowei returned to the study to grade the test papers herself. With a red pen, she marked each question on the printed papers as right or wrong, then turned back to the textbooks and notes to analyze the root causes of the errors: conceptual confusion, calculation mistakes, or misreading the questions. For the question types she repeatedly got wrong, she rewrote the relevant knowledge points and stuck them on a prominent spot on the bookshelf with sticky notes. This process lasted nearly three hours.

events.name: Focused topical review and monthly plan
events.description: At 7 p.m., Yu Xiaowei categorized all the wrong questions into a themed intensive checklist, including five major sections such as optimal portfolio allocation and tax-deferred instruments. Then she opened a new notebook and made a detailed study plan from October until two weeks before the exam, specifying the study content for each day's commute and lunch break, the weekly number of questions to complete, and the dates of two mock exams. Her husband Zhang Weiming dressed their son Zhang Zixuan in a white shirt and dark blue trousers, and put a white bow headband and a fluffy skirt on their daughter Zhang Yuxin. The family of four tidied their appearance in front of the entryway mirror, and Zhang Weiming gave a thumbs-up to show they were ready.

She warmly greeted the parents of her distant cousin Chen Jiamin, helped guide a few relatives who had gotten lost to their seats, and chatted with distant relatives she had not seen for a long time. Her husband Zhang Weiming, holding their son with one hand and their daughter in his other arm, talked softly with them nearby. The wedding was held as a warm Western-style ceremony. At the moment when the groom put the ring on the bride under the flower arch, Yu Xiaowei watched attentively throughout and snapped several photos. During the subsequent toasting session, she raised her champagne glass to offer sincere blessings to the couple. Seeing her cousin's happy smile, she secretly hoped that her daughter would one day have such a beautiful wedding.

After getting home, she cropped a group photo of the extended family and set it as her phone wallpaper, and said softly to Zhang Weiming, who was hanging up his coat: 'Jiamin, who we used to play with as kids, is married now. Time really flies.' She did this to remind herself of the preciousness of family bonds.

2025-09.daily_overview: In her first full marathon, Yu Xiaowei overcame cramps to finish the race with difficulty. Her family waited at the finish line and gave her tremendous support. After the race, she posted her reflections, and the family's emotional bond was strengthened.

events.name: Departing in the early morning for the starting point.
events.description: Woke up at 4 a.m., washed up, changed into running clothes, and checked the race bib, running shoes, and energy gels. Did 15 minutes of dynamic stretching in the living room and ate a banana. Left home at 5 and took a taxi to the Western Harbour Crossing Kowloon Toll Plaza starting point.

events.name: Full marathon race process
events.description: Arrived at the starting point at 5:30 and exchanged encouragement with fellow runner Shen Peiwen. The race started with the gun at 6:00. She advanced steadily at a pace of 6:10/km, passing through the Western Harbour Tunnel and the Central waterfront. By 8:45 she had reached the halfway point and felt good. After 25 km she entered Sham Shui Po. At 30 km, her hamstring suddenly cramped, forcing her to stop and walk. She replenished electrolytes and stretched, but the cramp kept recurring, so she could only alternate between running and walking. Relying on sheer willpower, she crossed the finish line at Victoria Park at 11:28 with a time of 5 hours 28 minutes. She received the finisher's medal and was helped by volunteers to the recovery area.

events.name: Family members waiting at the finish line.
events.description: At 11:40, Yu Xiaowei met her waiting husband Zhang Weiming, son, and daughter in the rest area. Zhang Weiming handed her water and a towel; her son waved a small flag and cheered; her daughter hugged her tightly and said, 'Mom is amazing.' The family took a photo at the finish line, and Zhang Weiming had also prepared pineapple buns and milk tea.

events.name: Return home to rest and share after the race.
events.description: At 2 p.m., she went home, took a cold shower, did some simple stretching, and ate the wonton noodles her mother had prepared to replenish her energy. At 8 p.m., she posted about her first marathon experience in the Hong Kong Streetathon running group: "A full marathon is like life; only after falling apart do you know you can persevere." She attached a finish-line photo. The group responded enthusiastically, and Shen Peiwen shared a photo of the two of them running together. She fell asleep before 22:00.

start_state.mood: Excited

end_state.mood: Extremely proud but physically exhausted

The family of four went to the nearby community hall for the weekend parent-child carnival. On the way, the children excitedly discussed the performances. Yu Xiaowei felt gratified for her children, but amid the applause she suddenly remembered the cold war with her father and the estrangement from her best friend; her smile did not reach her eyes. Yu Xiaowei quickly said it was no problem, and they arranged to meet sometime next week. After the short call, Yu Xiaowei felt the heavy stone in her heart lift a little.

2025-06.daily_overview: On Saturday, Yu Xiaowei's family threw themselves into the children's room renovation battle and completed the makeover amid laughter and joy. However, in the evening, her father had an emotional breakdown over a small matter, casting a shadow over the family atmosphere.

events.name: Early morning yoga
events.description: At 6:30 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei got up on time, spread out her yoga mat in front of the floor-to-ceiling window in the living room of her home in Kowloon City District, and did 15 minutes of breathing and stretching exercises to start an energetic day.

events.name: Children's room renovation preparation
events.description: That morning, the family of four worked together to move the movable furniture from the children's room to the living room, covered the bed and desk that could not be moved with old sheets, and swept the dust off the floor. Yu Xiaowei carefully applied painter's tape along the edges of the walls, door and window frames, and skirting boards to prevent paint drips; Zhang Weiming, meanwhile, used a stirring stick on the balcony to thoroughly mix the light-blue eco-friendly latex paint and poured it into the roller tray.

events.name: The Whole Family Had Fun Painting
events.description: In the morning, painting began. Zhang Weiming used a large roller to paint the upper walls, Yu Xiaowei used a brush to touch up the corners, and Zhang Zixuan and Zhang Yuxin excitedly applied paint to the lower walls with small rollers. Although quite a bit of paint was dripped and spilled, the family was full of laughter and the atmosphere was cheerful. Midway, the siblings argued over the shade of color, but after Yu Xiaowei gently mediated, the two worked together again.

events.name: Completion and decoration
events.description: After the painting was finished, the children took the initiative to suggest putting star stickers on the fully dried wall as decoration. Yu Xiaowei and Zhang Weiming helped secure the positions. Then the family packed up the tools together, washed the brushes, and moved the furniture back to its original place, making the children's room look brand new. The family lay on the new floor and celebrated.

events.name: Father Yu Guoqiang had an emotional outburst
events.description: At 4:00 p.m., father Yu Guoqiang came back from playing chess at the community park with a livid face. Mother Chen Meiling asked what was wrong, and father suddenly flew into a rage, saying his old chess buddy had been playing unfairly and that he had been mocked for making a bad move. At dinner, he shut himself in his room and refused to communicate with the family. Yu Xiaowei looked at her mother with concern, realizing that her father's emotional problems might not be entirely about father-daughter conflicts but had deeper causes. She decided she must arrange for her father to see a doctor soon.

events.name: Communicated with younger brother about father's condition.
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei comforted her mother and sent a WeChat message to her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng about their father's condition. Her brother suggested observing for a few days and, if it didn't improve, taking him to the psychology clinic. She sat in the living room, looking at the newly renovated children's room, silently hoping her father would also move past this dark period. Before bed, she completed 15 minutes of meditation, but her thoughts were still with her father.

start_state.mood: Energetic

end_state.location: Home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

2025-06.daily_overview: On Sunday, Yu Xiaowei finished yoga and her morning run. In the morning she did a makeup core-training session with Shen Peiwen over video, then conducted the monthly financial review with her husband. At noon, her son brought home his final report card and the whole family celebrated. In the afternoon she took the children to the community playground. In the evening she enjoyed quiet family time and completed the monthly diet review.

events.name: Morning yoga and morning jog.
events.description: At 5:45 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei got up, drank water, then did a 15-minute yoga warm-up in the living room. At 6:10 she went out for an easy 3 km jog on the community jogging path at a pace of 7:30/km, keeping her heart rate at 140, and did a full 10-minute stretch afterward. With running back in her routine, she felt her aerobic capacity gradually rebuilding.

events.name: Catch-up video core workout with Shen Peiwen.
events.description: At 10:00 a.m., Yu Xiaowei and Shen Peiwen did a video call via WeChat from their respective homes to make up for the core workout missed this week, including crunches, plank variations, etc., lasting 30 minutes. During the workout, Shen Peiwen shared the specific date of her upcoming trip to Singapore, and the two agreed to meet up before she left.

events.name: Monthly financial review
events.description: At 10:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming conducted a monthly financial review in the living room. They opened the family ledger: May balance, HK$1,500 deposited into the travel fund, and HK$2,000 invested monthly in the money market fund. Based on June expenses and the expectation that her husband would leave his job at the end of July, she suggested cutting the dining-out budget by another HK$3,000 in July and pausing travel fund deposits for three months. Her husband suggested first suspending his own coffee allowance. Yu Xiaowei smiled and said he didn't have to be that miserable. In the end, they decided to set aside HK$10,000 from the flexible fund as an emergency supplement.

events.name: Son's end-of-term report card
events.description: At noon, her son Zhang Zixuan received his end-of-term report card from school: Math A, Chinese B+, English B, an improvement over last semester. The whole family was happy. Yu Xiaowei kept her promise and rewarded him with a set of Lego bricks. Her son immediately opened it and started building.

events.name: Monthly diet review and planning
events.description: After breakfast, Yu Xiaowei completed the last day's food diary on her nutrition management app (breakfast: Hong Kong-style milk tea and pineapple bun; lunch: homemade bento — stir-fried chicken breast with broccoli and brown rice; dinner: at home — steamed sea bass, garlic lettuce, and millet porridge). She exported this month's diet report and found that her overall calorie intake was well controlled and protein intake met the target, but her vegetable variety was a bit limited. Based on this, she planned to add more leafy greens next month and planned to introduce a new healthy menu in July.

events.name: Parent-child time at the community playground.
events.description: At 4:00 p.m., the sudden rain had just stopped. Yu Xiaowei took her two children to the community playground. She watched her son climb the climbing frame and her daughter swing on the swing, while she sat on a bench replying to some non-urgent client messages on WeChat, enjoying a rare moment of leisure.

events.name: Family dinner and planning next week
events.description: In the evening, mother Chen Meiling made dumplings that the whole family loves. The family ate and chatted. Yu Xiaowei mentioned that she would start leading the team to sprint forward next week, and her husband said he would go to a new place to try out a job next week. Everyone encouraged each other.

events.name: Evening meditation and stretching
events.description: Before bed, completed a 10-minute full-body stretch and 15-minute mindfulness meditation, and fell asleep with a sense of fulfillment.

events.description: At 6:30 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei laid out her yoga mat in front of the living room floor-to-ceiling window and did 15 minutes of breathing and stretching exercises, gently waking up her body to start the new day.

events.name: Fragmented core training
events.description: After yoga, I completed a 5-minute plank and bird dog circuit; my core strength can easily handle it now.

events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowei received the June payslip through the company's internal payroll system at the AIA Hong Kong Wan Chai district office. She carefully checked the base salary adjustment after the promotion and the renewal performance bonus completed in May, calculated that the total had increased by about HK$8,000 compared with last month, and confirmed it was correct.

events.name: Led the team weekly meeting and announced new measures.
events.description: At 10:00 a.m., Yu Xiaowei led the team weekly meeting, officially announced that starting in July, new management measures would be implemented: daily 15-minute one-on-one communication and task templates, and showed the standardized task assignment table she had created. Team members accepted it, and He Junwen also nodded in agreement. Su Lishan immediately said she would help with the implementation.

events.name: Lunch and sharing with colleagues
events.description: At noon, Yu Xiaowei had lunch with Su Lishan at a cha chaan teng near the company, sharing the joy of a small salary increase. After congratulating her, Su Lishan joked that she deserved a raise too. The two also exchanged some management insights.

events.name: Client follow-ups and industry networking.
events.description: In the afternoon, she handled follow-up services for several policies and called a mainland peer she had met at the summit, agreeing to refer clients to each other next month. She also entered the potential client information introduced by Zhou Minyi into the system and set a follow-up reminder for next week.

events.name: Family financial transfers and spending time with the kids.
events.description: After work, Yu Xiaowei, at her home in Kowloon City District, used mobile banking to transfer 5,000 Hong Kong dollars into the joint family savings account for the family's medium- and long-term savings goals. She then transferred the remaining roughly 3,000 Hong Kong dollars to the daily household account to supplement this month's household expense budget. After that, she played jigsaw puzzles with the children in the living room for a while.

events.name: Health review and fasting plan
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei used the nutrition management app at home to check her dietary record report for the past 30 days. She found that her average daily calorie intake was controlled at around 1,800 kcal, protein intake had increased from 15% to 22%, and fruit and vegetable intake had clearly increased. Combining this with how she felt, she noticed that she had more energy during the day and was significantly less sleepy in the afternoon, while her weight had dropped about 1 kg to 54.8 kg. She saved a screenshot of the monthly summary in the app and shared it with her husband and mother in the family WeChat group, receiving encouragement from her family. She then planned to continue using the app in July and add a weekly 16:8 intermittent fasting attempt to slim down. The whole review process lasted about 40 minutes, during which she drank honey lemon water and recorded her personal reflections.

events.name: Heart-to-heart talk with husband before bed
events.description: Before bed, she talked with her husband Zhang Weiming about future plans. Her husband said he would try out at the new place tomorrow. Yu Xiaowei encouraged him and said that no matter the outcome, it was a good start. Afterward, she completed 15 minutes of mindfulness meditation and fell asleep peacefully.

2025-12.daily_overview: Today was the 66th birthday of her father, Yu Guoqiang. Yu Xiaowei still got up early and jogged 4 kilometers near home (at a 6:00 pace) as a way to wake up her body. During the day she stayed at her post and, after handling the last group insurance policy endorsement, left work an hour early. In the evening, the family of five gathered at the long-established Fung Shing Restaurant in Kowloon City, where the table was full of dishes her father loved. She put a scarf on her father with her own hands and gave him a red envelope, and their grandchildren laughed and gathered around him. Although her father still sighed occasionally about the investment matter, the mood at the dinner table gradually warmed. Yu Xiaowei voluntarily brought up her promise to change the wealth management plan, and her father finally loosened his stance. The whole family raised their glasses, and much of the gloom lifted. After the run her body was relaxed, but the sumptuous birthday feast made her weight increase slightly.

2025-12.daily_overview: Today marks a milestone on Yu Xiaowei's path of passing on Cantonese embroidery. She got up at 5:45 in the morning, did some simple yoga stretches, and at 8 o'clock went with He Meiling to the community center to set up the venue, turning the classroom into a small Cantonese embroidery exhibition hall. The introductory sharing class in the afternoon attracted about 20 trainees; she led the lecture on history and stitching techniques, with He Meiling assisting. What surprised her most was that Master Wu Xiuying came in person and, at the end of the class, publicly handed her the key to the studio, entrusting her with the important task of carrying on the craft; after class, Master Wu also urged her to sign up for the traditional crafts exhibition in March 2026 and asked her to complete the embroidery piece 'Winter'. Yu Xiaowei's voice choked up, and she was too excited to sleep all night. Because she stood all day, her step count exceeded 10,000, but she had no systematic training, went to bed late, and her weight dropped slightly.

events.name: Set up the venue for the sharing session
events.description: Starting at 9 a.m., she and He Meiling set up 12 long tables at the community center. On each table they placed embroidery material kits, small hoops, and practice cloth. Works such as Yu Xiaowei's “Peony” and “Spring” were displayed on the wall, and after adjusting the projector, clips of a Cantonese embroidery documentary were played on a loop.

events.name: Host an introductory Cantonese embroidery sharing class
events.description: From 2 to 4:30 PM, introduced participants to the century-long history of Cantonese embroidery in Cantonese, demonstrated the difference between the even stitch and the long-and-short stitch, and personally taught a silver-haired woman how to split silk threads. The class was lively, and the children were quietly threading needles.

events.name: Received the studio key and registered for the crafts exhibition.
events.description: At the end of the class, Teacher Wu Xiuying stepped forward, placed the brass key in Yu Xiaowei's hand, and said, 'From now on, the studio is your creative base.' Then Teacher Wu handed over the registration form for the crafts exhibition. Yu Xiaowei filled it out with tears in her eyes and promised to complete 'Winter' as soon as possible.

events.name: Post a social media update.
events.description: After returning home in the evening, I arranged the class photos, the close-up of the key, and the registration form into a nine-grid collage and posted it on Instagram and WeChat Moments, with the caption “Passing on the tradition is not one person’s job; starting today, I have taken on an extra sweet debt.” It received countless likes.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City

2025-12.daily_overview: Today was an important milestone in her career. She still tried to get up early to exercise, but after getting up at 6 a.m., she felt a slight discomfort in her stomach, so she only did 10 minutes of breathing meditation. At 10 a.m., she gave her year-end report to Liang Zhenhua, frankly presenting the fact that the team had achieved 112% of its performance target but ranked fourth in the region, without avoiding the mistakes in the Shenzhen market strategy or the risk of internal clients being poached. Liang Zhenhua affirmed her execution ability, but still decided to postpone the regional manager selection to June or July next year, asking her to deeply cultivate local high-end clients. After the report, she sat quietly in her office for half an hour, then calmly decided to suspend the Shenzhen business and focus on Hong Kong. When she returned home in the evening, she deliberately detoured to Kowloon City Market to buy roast pork and roast goose, comforting herself with good food. Due to her low mood and the comfort of eating, her weight continued to rise slightly.

She quickly transferred money to the family emergency reserve, paid the final installment for the massage chair, and shared the financial update with her husband. In the afternoon, she worked at her desk drafting a client protection process. In the evening, she braved the cold to go to Teacher Wu's studio in Sham Shui Po to learn snow-scene techniques. Teacher Wu taught her step by step how to lay stitches for snowflakes and create transitions between solid and soft areas. She practiced on the spot until 11 p.m. and left with red eyes but a heart full of joy—the crystal-like snowflake was blooming on the embroidery fabric. Feeling tired at night due to the skin discomfort and stress, she went to bed late, and her weight dropped slightly because of irregular eating.

At the morning meeting, the client registration process was officially announced, and Su Lishan took the lead in expressing her compliance. After the meeting, she hurriedly took the MTR to Mong Kok, where she met her father and Manager Li Guodong at the HSBC branch. In 40 minutes, she converted three high-risk funds in her father's account into conservative money-market funds and a six-month fixed deposit, with a total value of about HK$180,000. Her father signed a power of attorney on the spot allowing her to view the account. By the time everything was done, it was nearly noon, so she took her father to a teahouse next to the bank for shrimp dumplings and siu mai. Her father seemed much more relaxed. After returning home in the afternoon, she organized and filed the confirmation forms. In the evening, she focused on framing the 'Peony Painting' and raced to prepare promotional materials for the next day's charity sale until 11 p.m. Due to overwork and skin discomfort, her weight dropped slightly.

events.name: Announced the client reporting process at the morning meeting.

Su Lishan and the new employees all expressed understanding. After Li Xiaoming repeated the rules, everyone applauded and passed them.

Yu Xiaowei explained the fees and risk levels item by item, and her father nodded repeatedly. Finally, they additionally signed the account inquiry authorization letter.

events.name: Wealth management follow-up and lunch.
events.description: After finishing the errand, the father and daughter walked to a nearby London Restaurant for yum cha. Her father took the initiative to say, “From now on, I’ll ask you before buying anything.” Yu Xiaowei picked up a siu mai for him and said with a smile, “That’s the way.” The two were rarely so harmonious.

events.description: Returned home at 2 p.m., scanned the bank receipt and a copy of the authorization letter into the computer, and locked the originals in the drawer. Then I sent a WeChat voice message to my mother, Chen Meiling, briefly explaining the situation. She replied, "Amitabha, your father finally listened."

2025-12.daily_overview: Cantonese embroidery charity sale day. At 8 a.m., Yu Xiaowei met He Meiling and Wu Xiuying at the community center. The three took an hour to set up an elegant booth, and dozens of Cantonese embroidery pieces shone brightly under the lights. At 10 a.m., neighbors began to stream in. Yu Xiaowei vividly narrated the story behind each work to those who stopped to look. At 3 p.m., an elderly overseas Chinese with white hair stood before the Peony Painting, gazing at it for a long time, and finally offered HK$5,000 to buy it. He held Yu Xiaowei's hand and said, 'Looking at this embroidered piece reminds me of my grandma.' Teacher Wu Xiuying said with tears in her eyes, 'Only when a craft carries warmth can it be passed down.' The charity sale ended at 6 p.m., with 25 pieces sold and HK$28,000 raised. Yu Xiaowei carefully recorded every payment. After the event, she reviewed with He Meiling, tired but immensely satisfied. Because she was devoted all day, she only ate some snacks and did not drink enough water; her weight dropped slightly, but the red spots on her skin were more visible due to fatigue.

events.name: Setting up the charity sale booth in the early morning
events.description: Set off at 7:30, hung up the Cantonese Embroidery with Love · Charity Sale banner in the center lobby, arranged the exhibited works by theme into flower, figure, and animal sections, and placed a creation description card beside each piece. She deliberately put the Peony Painting in the most conspicuous spot near the entrance.

events.name: Explained Yue embroidery culture to visitors.
events.description: From 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., she served as the lead docent, introducing the history of Cantonese embroidery to different age groups, and threaded a needle on site to draw the children's attention. A middle school teacher made an on-the-spot booking for a lecture during the school's next Culture Week.

events.name: Peony Painting sold at a high price and interaction with an elderly overseas Chinese.
events.description: At 3 p.m., an elderly overseas Chinese man in his 70s, Uncle Chen, stood in front of the Peony Painting for half an hour. Yu Xiaowei told him that she had used more than ten kinds of red silk thread to bring out the layers of the peonies. Uncle Chen eventually bought it for HK$5,000 and asked to take a photo with the creator. This made the whole room burst into applause.

events.name: Teacher Wu Xiuying's touching message
events.description: After the deal was successfully completed, Wu Xiuying held Yu Xiaowei's hand and said in front of everyone, “You have given these threads a soul. I remember you now. This is how craftsmanship keeps its warmth from generation to generation.” Yu Xiaowei bowed deeply.

events.name: Event wrap-up and review
events.description: At 6 p.m. they closed the stall, and she counted the cash with He Meiling: total receipts were HK$28,500. She immediately took a photo with the foundation's promotional flyer and sent it via WeChat to Huang Wenhui to share the good news. The two sat on cardboard boxes, eating pineapple buns to regain their energy, and agreed to do it again next year.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City

2025-12.daily_overview: On Sunday morning, Yu Xiaowei honored the agreement she had made with her body. She got up at 7, put on her new Nike running shoes, and completed a 10 km morning run along the jogging trail in Kowloon Tsai Park, keeping the pace at around 5:30 per kilometer with good heart rate zone control. It was her first long-distance recovery run after her half-marathon PB in November. After the run, she did a full set of yoga stretches on the lawn, which took 25 minutes. Then she sat on a bench and used her phone's notes app to plan her full-marathon training plan for the first quarter of 2026. After returning home and showering, she synced her workout data to her Garmin account and smiled with satisfaction at the graphs. In the afternoon, she curled up on the sofa watching cartoons with her daughter. In the evening, the family went to try a newly opened Vietnamese pho restaurant—a rare chance to relax. Because of heavy sweating and a balanced diet, her weight dropped slightly, and the skin redness was mildly irritated by sweat from exercise, but she felt happy.

events.description: Arrived at the park at 7:40 a.m. and completed 10 km in 4 laps at a pace of 5:30 per kilometer. Her heart rate stayed at 145-155 bpm throughout. She felt her breathing was smooth, her legs had no soreness, and her fitness had recovered well.

events.name: Post-run yoga stretching and writing the plan

Then she used her memo app to outline her full marathon training plan: W1-W4 base phase, W5-W8 build phase, W9-W12 adjustment phase, and resolved to register for the 2026 Standard Chartered Full Marathon.

events.name: Workout data sync and analysis
events.description: At 10 o'clock, I went home, opened Garmin Connect, and checked the split pace, cadence, and vertical oscillation in detail, adding the note "A long-awaited 10K; my feet still remember the way." I shared the data to the running group, and Shen Peiwen instantly replied with a thumbs-up.

In the evening, the couple walked with the children to Yueweixuan at the corner of the street, where the family shared rare and well-done beef pho and spring rolls, and her husband specially ordered a salted lemon 7-Up for her.

2025-12.daily_overview: Today Yu Xiaowei completed the full circle of a good deed and also faced a cold confrontation over friendship. In the morning, she took the 28,500 Hong Kong dollars raised from yesterday's charity sale to the Hong Kong Children's Cancer Foundation office in Central, donated it solemnly in the name of all three, and sent a photo of the thank-you letter to Teacher Wu and He Meiling. In the afternoon, unable to bear the suspicion in her heart any longer, she met her best friend Zhou Minyi at Pacific Coffee on Prince Edward Road West and directly brought up the matter of client Wang Qiming being signed away. Zhou Minyi argued that clients naturally compare prices and she could not interfere. Yu Xiaowei did not press further, but both knew the trust was shattered. When they parted, Zhou Minyi whispered, "It wasn't my intention," and Yu Xiaowei only replied, "I know." In the evening, she went home alone and silently set Zhou Minyi's WeChat to Do Not Disturb. She was wrapped in exhaustion, but when she saw the Christmas card her daughter had drawn at dinner, she decided to look only forward. Because of her low spirits, she had little appetite at dinner, and her weight crept back up to 53.1 kg. The red skin spots had not faded, and she applied repair cream before bed.

events.name: Proceeds from the charity sale
events.description: At 10 a.m., I went to the foundation office at 3 Garden Road, Central, handed the envelope containing cash to the finance officer, and made a donation in the names of Yu Xiaowei, He Meiling, and Wu Xiuying to support art therapy for children with cancer. I received a thank-you certificate printed with the foundation's LOGO.

events.name: Share donation results in the group
events.description: After leaving the foundation, she sat at a nearby Starbucks and posted the donation certificate and yesterday's lively charity sale scenes to the three-person Cantonese embroidery group. Wu Xiuying replied with a voice message, 'Good, good, good, I'm proud of you,' and He Meiling sent a crying emoji.

events.name: Meet with Zhou Minyi and confront her directly.
events.description: At 3 p.m., she ordered two cups of hot milk tea at the cafe. Once Zhou Minyi sat down, she skipped the small talk and went straight to the point: “Last month, for Wang Qiming's group insurance, did you give another agent an internal quote?” Zhou Minyi's face went pale, and then she explained that the client had asked to compare quotes from several companies, and she had only provided the standard rate.

events.name: The relationship appears broken on the surface
events.description: The conversation lasted less than 20 minutes before the two reached an impasse. Before leaving, Zhou Minyi said softly, "It wasn't my intention." Yu Xiaowei turned her head away and murmured, "I know," watching out the window until the other had walked away. She felt a sense of loss and, in her memory, drew a full stop to this 15-year friendship.

events.name: Processing emotions after returning home.
events.description: Returning home in the evening, she deliberately did not mention the matter. Seeing the Christmas card her daughter had drawn at the dining table (showing the family and a cat), she felt a lump in her throat and patted her daughter's head. She then muted Zhou Minyi on WeChat, deciding to keep only surface courtesy in the future.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City

events.description: Went to the dermatology department at Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital. After asking about her recent skin care habits, the doctor said that stopping the exfoliating scrub on December 10 was correct, but the frequent makeup and makeup removal, plus the combined use of multiple cleansing products while preparing for the sharing session and charity sale, were the real cause of the damaged skin barrier. The doctor diagnosed it as barrier damage caused by stress and over-cleansing, prescribed a medical repair cream, and advised avoiding strong cleansing.

2025-12.daily_overview: The health check-up sounded a health alarm, revealing that long-term stress had caused elevated cortisol and excess stomach acid, which was linked to the previous skin allergy issues. events.name: Discussing the medical report with Dr. Zhou Wenbin
events.description: The doctor pointed out elevated cortisol and early excess stomach acid, and advised reducing caffeine, increasing aerobic exercise, and ensuring 7 hours of sleep. Dr. Zhou turned to the record of the skin allergy in December and said, “Look, the body’s signals are connected. Your elevated cortisol, excess stomach acid, and the earlier impaired skin barrier all point to the same problem — pushing yourself too hard. Luckily, it’s not too late for you to adjust now.” He also praised her perseverance in maintaining her habits.

2025-03.daily_overview: On Wednesday, Yu Xiaowei went to Shenzhen for a cross-border insurance sharing session and secured a cooperation intention for group health insurance. In the evening, she had a warm dinner with family and friends. Her cross-border business has officially begun; although tiring, it was rewarding.

events.name: Morning simplified yoga and meditation (early wake-up).
events.description: At 5:45 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei got up and shortened her yoga and meditation to 10 minutes to make time for the cross-border trip.

events.name: Cross-border trip to Shenzhen.
events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowei set off from home, took a cross-border direct bus via Shenzhen Bay Port, and, after a ride of about one hour, arrived at the Science and Technology Park in Nanshan District, Shenzhen, reaching the area near Tencent Building around 11:00 a.m.

events.name: Host a cross-border insurance sharing session.
events.description: Yu Xiaowei held a small cross-border insurance sharing session in a booked meeting room at Tencent Building for about 12 potential clients. Drawing on her own experience, she explained in detail the advantages of Hong Kong insurance, such as multi-currency policies, high-end medical insurance, and savings with dividends, as well as cross-border asset allocation solutions for high-net-worth individuals from the mainland, and used real cases to answer questions.

events.name: Had an in-depth talk with client Wang Qiming.
events.description: After the sharing session, Yu Xiaowei had an in-depth one-hour meeting with Wang Qiming at a cafe near the building. Wang Qiming consulted on cross-border group health insurance and customized personal high-end medical plans for his company's executive team. Yu Xiaowei initially designed several plans, and the two reached a preliminary intention to cooperate on the premiums, coverage, and claims process for group health insurance, agreeing to submit a formal quotation later. Wang Qiming also revealed that the company's executives were interested in personal high-end medical insurance, but it would need to be discussed in detail after the group insurance was finalized.

events.name: Dining with family and friends
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei had a gathering at a Hong Kong-style tea restaurant near Nanshan District's Science and Technology Park with her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng, close friend Huang Wenhui, and embroidery friend He Meiling. During the meal, everyone shared updates. Yu Xiaowei gave each person a small piece of Cantonese embroidery she had stitched by hand; her brother talked about Tencent's new project; Huang Wenhui shared about life in Shenzhen; He Meiling talked about her latest works. The atmosphere was warm, and the gathering ended around 8 p.m.

events.name: Returning to Hong Kong and organizing memos
events.description: After the dinner gathering, Yu Xiaowei took the cross-border direct bus back to Hong Kong at 8:30 p.m. and arrived home on Prince Edward Road at about 10:00. After getting home, she briefly recorded the key points of the trip and organized the intent to cooperate with Wang Qiming into a memorandum, ready to report the next day.

start_state.mood: Slightly nervous but full of drive

end_state.location: At home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District

2025-03.daily_overview: After completing morning yoga on Sunday morning, Yu Xiaowei decided to suspend the scheduled long-distance training because her right knee still had slight soreness, and instead devoted herself to spring family cleaning with her husband. The two thoroughly cleaned the storage room, sorted items, and repaired the loose partition board. In the afternoon they took donated items to the community thrift store, and in the evening the whole family enjoyed the tidy home environment. The knee discomfort eased slightly after rest.

events.name: Morning yoga and family breakfast
events.description: At 6:30 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei spread out her yoga mat on the living room balcony and completed 15 minutes of Surya Namaskar yoga and 5 minutes of meditation. Her right knee still felt a slight pulling pain when she did Warrior Pose, so she chose to reduce the range. Then she prepared breakfast for the family: pineapple buns with butter, fried eggs, and hot milk tea. Her husband Zhang Weiming helped the children get up. The whole family ate together in a warm atmosphere.

events.name: Preparing for the big clean-up and discussing how to divide the work
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei and her husband counted cleaning tools outside the storage room and briefly discussed the division of work: Yu Xiaowei was responsible for sorting items and cleaning, while Zhang Weiming was responsible for checking and repairing the shelves. She specifically mentioned her knee discomfort, so her husband took charge of high places and heavy lifting.

events.name: Moving out items and initial cleaning
events.description: The two moved all the items in the storage room to the living room floor one by one. Zhang Weiming wiped the partitions, walls, and floor with a cloth; Yu Xiaowei swept the corners with a broom while keeping her knees only slightly bent. Discarded clutter was temporarily put into garbage bags, and the cleanup lasted about 40 minutes.

events.name: Sorting and Packing Items
events.description: On the living room carpet, Yu Xiaowei and Zhang Weiming checked the usefulness and condition of each item. Items that were intact but no longer needed were categorized as donations; damaged items were categorized as discards; and items to keep were stored in cardboard boxes. Yu Xiaowei packed them separately in cardboard boxes and trash bags, while Zhang Weiming checked the list.

events.name: Repair the partition board in the storage room.
events.description: After sorting was done, Zhang Weiming took out a screwdriver, wood glue, and screws, disassembled the loose shelf board, and reinforced it. Yu Xiaowei handed him tools and helped steady the board. The repair took about 20 minutes.

events.name: Putting things back in place and tidying up
events.description: After the repair was finished, the two of them put the items to be kept back into the storage room according to the new layout. Heavy items were placed on the bottom, seasonal clothing and travel items on the top, and tools and documents were put into labeled storage bins. Yu Xiaowei handed over and arranged items while Zhang Weiming adjusted their stability; in the end, the storage room was neat and orderly.

events.name: Donated items sent to the community secondhand store.
events.description: After finishing the tidying, Yu Xiaowei loaded the donation boxes into her family car and drove with Zhang Weiming to a community thrift store in Kowloon City District. At the store, they counted the items and handed them to the staff, filled out a donation registration form, and received a receipt, then drove home. Her knees felt slightly tired after the moving, so she applied an ice pack for 10 minutes after getting home.

events.name: Changed into a white shirt and dress pants, checked my briefcase, then said goodbye to my family. On the way, I chose to play soft piano music, closed my eyes to rest, emptied my mind, and prepared for work.
events.description: At 6:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei felt a bit groggy from last night's hangover but still managed to complete 15 minutes of yoga meditation. She then organized her Cantonese embroidery kit and prepared a simple breakfast for the family. She set out for Sham Shui Po before 9 o'clock.

events.name: Learning new stitching techniques in the advanced Cantonese embroidery class.

Yu Xiaowei practiced carefully, but she noticed that the students were mostly older, and the problem of passing on the traditional craft was emerging.

events.name: The teacher privately passed on her advice.
events.description: After the class, Teacher Wu Xiuying deliberately kept Yu Xiaowei behind, held her hand and sighed, 'Young people nowadays are less and less willing to learn; I'm really afraid this craft will be lost.' She then said softly, 'If one day I can no longer teach, I truly hope someone will take over this studio.' Yu Xiaowei was deeply moved, held the teacher's hand tightly, and promised to seriously consider it.

events.name: Family supermarket shopping in the afternoon

The children helped push the small shopping cart while she picked out salmon and vegetables on weekend special, planning a Sunday picnic. She felt tired and skipped the planned core training.

events.name: Evening solo practice and early sleep.
events.description: After the children fell asleep at night, Yu Xiaowei took out the embroidery frame in the study and practiced the layered stitch technique she had learned during the day for about 45 minutes, then photographed the embroidered piece and sent it to Teacher Wu for advice. Looking at the needle and thread, she felt a deep sense of responsibility for passing on the craft. Because she had been short on sleep for several days, she decided to go to bed at 10:30.

In the afternoon, she did mindful walking and meditation, and in the evening shared her inner insights. She completely put aside her phone and felt the tranquility. The light meals and inner reflection caused her weight to drop.

events.name: Departed for Sai Kung in the morning
events.description: At 8 a.m., Yu Xiaowei said goodbye to her family, took simple luggage, and took a taxi to the Sai Kung Seaside Retreat Center. events.name: Afternoon body scan meditation.

Yu Xiaowei spoke candidly about work pressure, family responsibilities, and her desire to "slow down." Hearing similar stories from others, she felt understood. At 10 p.m. she returned to her room to rest.

2025-04.daily_overview: The whole family went to Shenzhen to pay respects to their ancestors. After listening to family stories, Yu Xiaowei was deeply moved and felt nourished by the family's resilient spirit. Returning home in the evening, she organized her notes and turned this emotion into inner strength. Due to the tight schedule, she did not go running, but her walking steps exceeded 10,000.

events.name: Set off for Shenzhen in the early morning to pay respects at the grave.
events.description: At 6:00 a.m., all six family members set off from home, driving a seven-seater through Shenzhen Bay Port to Xili Cemetery. On the way, her father Yu Guoqiang again explained the order of the memorial ritual and the locations of the ancestral tombstones. Yu Xiaowei did a simplified meditation in the car to calm her emotions.

events.name: Ancestral grave worship and family stories
events.description: After arriving at the cemetery, the whole family placed offerings in front of the ancestral grave, burned incense, and bowed. Uncle Yu Guoliang recounted in detail the hardships of great-grandfather coming south from Guangzhou to Shenzhen to start from scratch. Grandmother Liang Shufang added details about how, in an era of scarce resources, great-grandmother supported five children through her Cantonese embroidery skills. Yu Xiaowei listened intently, feeling for the first time the connection between Cantonese embroidery and her own bloodline.

events.name: Family dinner and reflections on the return trip.
events.description: After the tomb-sweeping, the two families went to a Cantonese restaurant near the cemetery for a reunion lunch. During the meal, Grandma held Yu Xiaowei's hand and urged her to pass on the Cantonese embroidery craft. After saying goodbye, the whole family drove back to Hong Kong. On the way, Yu Xiaowei, her mother, and her husband talked about the resilience of the women in their family during turbulent times, and her mother Chen Meiling also recalled episodes of learning embroidery when she was young.

events.name: Organize family records and old belongings.
events.description: Back at home in Kowloon City in the evening, Yu Xiaowei recorded in her diary the family stories she had heard during the day, and looked through an old photo album her mother had found, which contained several yellowed photos of her grandmother's embroidery. She stroked the photos, her heart filled with a sense of connection across time and space, and decided to make Cantonese embroidery her spiritual anchor. Before going to bed, she leaned against the headboard and wrote down her reflections of the day, not resting until 11:30.
