events.name: Brief family time in the evening
events.description: At 6:30 p.m., her husband Zhang Weiming left work early and rushed to Kwun Tong to take over caring for the children, allowing Yu Xiaowei to go home ahead of time. She had dinner with her mother and the children, listened to her son talk about a small game in his football class, and her daughter showed off a craft made with stickers. She checked and signed the children’s homework, enjoying a short but precious parent-child moment.

events.name: Japanese review before bed was interrupted.
events.description: At 9 p.m., after the children fell asleep, Yu Xiaowei sat in the study and opened the recording of her Japanese lesson. She planned to study 50 minutes of new content, but after only 10 minutes her eyelids were growing heavy. Several nights of insufficient sleep made it impossible for her to concentrate. She helplessly turned off the video, did a simple 5-minute meditation, and decided to cut herself some slack for the moment.

events.name: Call reminder from younger brother Yu Xiaofeng
events.description: At 9:45 p.m., Yu Xiaowei received a video call from her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng, who was in Shenzhen. During the casual chat, her brother mentioned that their father had recently been asking relatives about investments and sounded very excited. Yu Xiaowei said she knew about it and would keep an eye on it, but inside she became more cautious.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Slightly tired but with clear goals; she has to balance work and caregiving, and her neck still feels uncomfortable.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: A touch of frustration at interrupted study, but daytime family time was comforting; she felt slightly uneasy about her father's movements.

state.daily_exercise: Morning yoga for 15 minutes; in spare moments, 2 sets of wall sits and 3 sets of bird-dog exercises.

date_attribute.weather: Cloudy, with brief sunny spells, 24-29°C, humidity 80%

2025-04.daily_overview: Family incidents came one after another: in the morning, her father suddenly came by and presented a high-risk investment proposal, putting Yu Xiaowei on alert; in the afternoon, the family cat Fatty slipped out in the chaos, causing the whole family to worry; in the evening, she finally decided to suspend the systematic Japanese course and switch to a fragmented self-study approach. It was an emotionally tense day, but amid the chaos she also made a pragmatic adjustment to her studies. The soreness in her neck improved slightly after repeated stretching.

events.name: Morning self-adjustment and reflection on transforming the learning model
events.description: At 5:40 am, Yu Xiaowei woke up on the fold-out bed in her mother-in-law's home where she was temporarily staying. After washing up briefly, she drank instant coffee and wrote a two-week study transition plan in the notes app on her phone. She decided no longer to force herself to keep up with the Japanese course, and instead planned to use fragmented time during commutes and lunch breaks to study, downloading apps such as Duolingo. While her mother-in-law was still asleep, she did 5 minutes of Vinyasa flow yoga to relax her body.

events.name: Deliver breakfast and arrange daytime care for mother-in-law
events.description: At 7 o'clock, she prepared cereal and a banana for her mother-in-law and contacted her neighbor Mrs. Ho to ask if she could help look after her during the day for two hours. Mrs. Ho readily agreed. Yu Xiaowei left her own mobile phone number and her family doctor's number, then hurried back to her own home.

events.name: Father Yu Guoqiang brought high-risk investment materials
events.description: At 10 a.m., while Yu Xiaowei was organizing the afternoon client materials at home, her father, Yu Guoqiang, came over from his home in Kowloon City, mysteriously pulled her onto the balcony, and took out a printed investment project document. The project claimed an annualized return of 12%, but after a quick skim, Yu Xiaowei saw that it was a high-risk local infrastructure private placement product with no compliant registration. She accepted the materials for now, saying she needed to study them further, but inwardly she was already convinced it was a scam and decided to find an opportunity to discuss it with her mother.

events.name: The family cat, Fatty, went missing.
events.description: At 12 noon, as Yu Xiaowei was about to leave, she found that the front door had not been closed tightly, and Feizai, the usually quiet orange cat, was missing. She immediately called her husband and children to search inside the house, then the whole family expanded the search to the stairwell and the community garden. The two children were so anxious that they burst into tears. Yu Xiaowei had her husband post cat-finding notices in the owners' group and on social media, while she personally put up 10 self-made posters in the community. But there was still no news by late night. During the search, she walked briskly nearly 10,000 steps, yet her anxiety did not ease.

events.name: Afternoon client phone follow-ups and formal suspension of Japanese lessons.
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei mustered her energy and called four long-time clients in the living room to remind them of their renewal premium payment dates. Then she sent a formal email to the Japanese language training institution requesting a three-month postponement of the course, and thanked them for their understanding. After discussing with her husband in the family WeChat group, she decided to adopt a fragmented self-study plan. That night, during the MTR commute, she used an app to memorize 15 kana characters.

events.name: In the evening, helped her husband with household chores.
events.description: At 6 p.m., feeling down about searching for the cat, Yu Xiaowei did not go to her mother-in-law's house (her husband was responsible for delivering dinner), but stayed home and prepared a simple dinner with her mother. After the meal, she washed the dishes, tidied the kitchen, checked all the doors and windows, and made a temporary barrier out of a cardboard box to prevent the cat from going out.

events.name: A brief conversation with her husband before bed
events.description: At 10 p.m., after the children had gone to bed, Yu Xiaowei and Zhang Weiming sat in the living room, discussing the possible reasons the cat had gone missing and comforting each other. Both said they had been under too much pressure lately and needed to support each other. Zhang Weiming offered to take full responsibility for her mother-in-law's lunch and dinner over the next two days so that Yu Xiaowei could rest.

start_state.location: The living room of the mother-in-law's home in Kwun Tong District.
start_state.mood: Woken from sleep by the alarm clock, groggy from lack of sleep, neck stiffness slightly reduced

end_state.location: Bedroom at home on Prince Edward Road West.
end_state.mood: Anxious and exhausted, under pressure from the cat's disappearance and her father's investment demands, but the couple encouraged each other.

state.daily_exercise: 5 minutes of morning vinyasa yoga, about 10,000 steps walking to search for the cat, and micro neck stretches

2025-04.daily_overview: On the weekend family day, Yu Xiaowei put aside all work and took the whole family to her mother-in-law's house for quality time. In the morning, her husband did the cooking and made soup, she handled cleaning and tidying, and the children chatted and drew with their grandmother. In the afternoon, she helped her mother-in-law organize the wardrobe while her husband fixed appliances. In the evening, the family had a warm dinner together, and everyone was relieved to hear that her mother-in-law's swelling had subsided. After returning home that night, she was still worried about the cat and went out alone before bed to search the neighborhood again. She exchanged a few words with her running buddy Shen Peiwen on her phone, and they agreed to resume Wednesday night runs once her mother-in-law recovered.

events.name: The whole family went to Kwun Tong to visit her mother-in-law.
events.description: At 8 a.m., Yu Xiaowei, her husband Zhang Weiming, their son Zhang Zixuan, and daughter Zhang Yuxin left their home on Prince Edward Road West and took a bus to her mother-in-law's place in Kwun Tong. Before leaving, she picked up the latest issue of Hong Kong Runner magazine from the lobby mailbox, planning to bring it to her mother-in-law to pass the time.

events.name: Husband prepared lunch for his mother.
events.description: At 10 a.m., Zhang Weiming was busy in the kitchen at his mother's home, with Yu Xiaowei assisting. They simmered his mother's favorite pork bone soup with green radish and carrot, and also steamed pork ribs and stir-fried choy sum. The smell of the soup lifted his mother's mood, and the swelling in her ankle had gone down a bit.

events.name: Yu Xiaowei helps her mother-in-law with housework.
events.description: After lunch at 1 p.m., Yu Xiaowei had her mother-in-law sit on the sofa with a magazine, and she began tidying up the messy wardrobe. She packed away winter clothes and hung spring everyday clothes in an easy-to-reach spot. She also changed the bed sheets and pillowcases, and wiped down the nightstand and remote control with disinfectant wipes. While tidying, she did a few squats and calf raises to maintain a little activity.

events.name: Husband repaired the ceiling lamp and checked the electrical circuits.
events.description: At 3 p.m., Zhang Weiming noticed an old chandelier in the living room flickering. He immediately went downstairs, bought a new ballast, and replaced it, while also checking all the outlets and switches in the house. Her mother-in-law praised him for being careful, and Yu Xiaowei also joked, "The handyman husband finally proves useful."

events.name: Setting small rehabilitation goals for her mother-in-law.
events.description: At 4:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowei checked her mother-in-law's ankle and found that the swelling had mostly subsided. She used her phone to look up simple ankle circles and toe curling exercises, taught them to her mother-in-law hands-on, and encouraged her to do them three times a day for five minutes each time. Although her mother-in-law grumbled that it was troublesome, she agreed with a smile.

events.name: Returned home after family dinner.
events.description: At 6 PM, Yu Xiaowei reheated the leftovers from lunch, and the family sat together to eat. Before leaving, she sorted her mother-in-law's medicine for the next three days into a pill organizer by morning, noon, and evening, and asked her neighbor Mrs. Ho to keep an eye on her. At 7:30, they took the bus home, and the children fell asleep on the bus from exhaustion.

events.name: Searching for the cat and evening phone call.
events.description: At 9 p.m., after returning home, Yu Xiaowei called her mother, Chen Meiling, to report that her mother-in-law was recovering well. After hanging up, she went downstairs alone and searched again around the community greenbelt, parking lot, and garbage station, calling Feizai's name, but only an echo answered. Feeling dejected, she returned home and updated the lost-cat post in the social group. Before bed, she exchanged a few encouraging messages with her running buddy Shen Peiwen on WeChat, who suggested that she take some time to do deep-breathing relaxation.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home on Prince Edward Road West.
start_state.mood: Woke up naturally on the weekend, got into the right frame of mind to prepare for family activities, and remained worried about the cat.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Felt warmth from the family gathering, but the cat's absence brought a touch of melancholy; contact with running friends slightly eased the loneliness.

state.daily_exercise: Daily household chores, a number of squats and calf raises, and a 30-minute evening walk around the neighborhood looking for the cat.

2025-04.daily_overview: Sunday was full of dramatic twists. She had a rare lie-in in the morning, but in the afternoon she faced her father's pressing investment demands, triggering intense moral anxiety; in the evening she fell into regret after impulsive shopping; at night she received the surprise of the cat coming home and deep emotional support from her husband. In one day, her mood soared from a low point to warm release, and the couple's relationship became unprecedentedly close through honest dialogue.

events.name: Morning housework and short mental break
events.description: At 8:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei woke up naturally. She had a simple breakfast of white congee and stir-fried noodles made by her mother, then washed the sports clothes that had accumulated over the week and put away the yoga mat in the living room. At 10 o'clock, she sat on the sofa drinking Hong Kong-style milk tea and let herself scroll through social media for half an hour. Seeing marathon photos shared by a former colleague, she felt a little envious, but her legs were itching to run after days of caregiving without running.

events.name: Father called to formally present his investment request
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei received a call from her father Yu Guoqiang. He said directly that he had his eye on that high-yield project and hoped she would support him with 150,000 Hong Kong dollars. Yu Xiaowei stalled, citing the family's recent large expenses, and her father's tone became dejected. After hanging up, she felt overwhelming pressure and knew that simply delaying would not solve the problem.

events.name: Mother privately told Father about the true motive
events.description: Half an hour later, her mother, Chen Meiling, quietly pulled Yu Xiaowei into the kitchen and told her that a few months ago, after her father had wanted to use his retirement pension to buy the latest game console for his grandson and had been turned down, he had kept saying that he was old and useless. This investment was actually his attempt to prove that he could still contribute to the family. Hearing this, Yu Xiaowei felt even more torn and could not bear to directly call it out.

events.name: Yu Xiaowei vaguely responded to her father, and her father mistakenly thought she agreed.
events.description: At 3 p.m., Yu Xiaowei returned to the living room and said to her father, "I'll go back and look into it more carefully and give you an answer in a few days." Her tone was hesitant, but she did not clearly object. Her father, Yu Guoqiang, visibly relaxed, slapped his thigh and said, "Then it's settled," and immediately called his son Yu Xiaofeng in Shenzhen to share the "good news." Yu Xiaofeng reminded him on the phone to be cautious, but the father dismissed it. Yu Xiaowei listened nearby, feeling tormented inside.

events.name: The cat Feizai returned on its own.
events.description: At 6:20 in the evening, just as the whole family was sunk in low spirits, a familiar meow came from outside the door. Yu Xiaowei opened the door and saw Fatty crouching at the doorstep, filthy and looking thinner, but seemingly unhurt. She picked the cat up excitedly, and the children cheered and jumped for joy. Yu Xiaowei immediately bathed and fed the cat, and after checking that there were no injuries, she held it in her arms and muttered, “Don't you ever run off again.” The gloom hanging over the family instantly lifted.

events.name: Impulse spending after stress relief
events.description: At 7 PM, Yu Xiaowei, overwhelmed by days of stress, broke down. Instead of going straight home to cook dinner, she walked alone to the Kowloon City mall to clear her mind. Passing a designer handbag store, she impulsively bought a designer handbag for 8,500 yuan. After swiping her card and looking at the bill, regret and anxiety surged over her. She sat blankly on a bench in the mall for a long while with the shopping bag.

events.name: Late-night couple talk and financial negotiation.
events.description: At 10:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowei got home, and her husband Zhang Weiming noticed her unusual expression and asked gently. She finally broke down crying, pouring out the exhaustion of caring for her mother-in-law, frustrations at work, and the pressure of her father's investment demands. Zhang Weiming did not blame her for the impulsive spending; instead, he held her in his arms to comfort her, proactively promised to take full responsibility for his mother's dinner and care for the next two days, and suggested that they re-plan the monthly budget together to bring shopping expenses under control, making up for it over the next few months by eating out less. Yu Xiaowei's emotions were fully accepted, and the couple's relationship became especially close because of this. Before bed, she did 10 minutes of stretching to relax.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home on Prince Edward Road West.
start_state.mood: After getting enough sleep, she felt somewhat better, but her father's matter still weighed on her mind.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Healed by her husband's understanding and the cat's return, her anxiety was relieved, and the couple's emotional bond deepened.

state.daily_exercise: In the evening, walked about 6,000 steps while shopping, and did 10 minutes of stretching before bed.

date_attribute.weather: Cloudy turning to thundershowers, 24-28°C, with brief strong winds

2025-04.daily_overview: On Monday, Yu Xiaowei switched to all-day rotation mode: in the morning she took her mother-in-law to her first physical therapy session and purchased rehabilitation aids; in the afternoon she returned to the company to handle customer complaints and backlogged work, with frustration building up; in the evening she worked overtime revising proposals until late at night, but was moved to tears by a loving crayon drawing from her daughter. The warm moment between father and daughter became the brightest light of today. Afterwards, the couple completed their monthly financial review and set up a new travel fund, injecting some order and hope into the chaotic April.

events.name: Accompanying her mother-in-law to her first physical therapy session.
events.description: At 8 a.m., after arranging for her husband to take the two children to school, Yu Xiaowei drove to Kwun Tong to pick up her mother-in-law and went to the community physiotherapy center. The therapist, Miss Chen, gave her mother-in-law a 15-minute massage and hot compress, then demonstrated exercises such as ankle pumps and seated heel raises. Yu Xiaowei recorded video and wrote down the key points in detail. While waiting, she did several sets of planks in the hallway.

events.name: Purchasing rehabilitation aids for her mother-in-law
events.description: After the treatment, Yu Xiaowei took her mother-in-law to a medical equipment store in Kowloon City and picked out a lightweight quad cane, two rolls of elastic bandages, and a pair of thermal knee pads. On the way, she also bought muscle-relief cream at the pharmacy across the street. The total cost was about 1,200 Hong Kong dollars. Back at her mother-in-law's home, she removed the small rugs that could cause tripping, moved the coffee table to a corner, and cleared an obstacle-free passage.

events.name: Returned to the company to handle a customer complaint
events.description: At 1:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowei rushed to the office in Wan Chai. As soon as she sat down, she received a call from a client, Chen Meiling, a full-time housewife who shared the same name as her mother. The client was agitated and accused the service of being poor because her husband's hospitalization medical claim had not been credited for two weeks. Yu Xiaowei immediately checked the system and found that the delay was due to a late submission of hospital materials. She patiently explained and promised to follow up personally, but after hanging up she felt deeply wronged and sat in her seat quietly wiping the corners of her eyes.

events.name: Look up her father's investment project information
events.description: At 3 p.m., after handling several policy renewals, Yu Xiaowei entered the project number provided by her father into the company's internal risk inquiry platform. The results showed that the product was not registered with the SFC, and the affiliated company had multiple complaint records. She saved a screenshot and decided she had to formally refuse her father within the week, but the thought of hurting his self-esteem made her feel guilty again.

events.name: Worked overtime to revise a client's insurance plan
events.description: At 6 p.m., after most colleagues had left work, Yu Xiaowei worked overtime alone in the office, revising a comprehensive plan for a potential high-end client that combined critical illness insurance and savings dividends. Applying the asset allocation theory she had just learned in her CFP course, she repeatedly adjusted the sum insured and premium payment period, striving to highlight the tax optimization value. During overtime, she stood up every half hour to do a set of neck and shoulder stretches.

events.name: Daughter gave a painting late at night, and her emotions overwhelmed her.
events.description: At 10:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowei returned home with her computer and continued revising the proposal in the study. Her 5-year-old daughter, Zhang Yuxin, gently pushed the door open and came in, holding a crayon drawing in both hands — it showed a big flower and a smiling mother, with 'Mom, keep going!' written crookedly below. Yu Xiaowei choked up at once and hugged her daughter tightly. The exhaustion and grievances accumulated over the past days melted away in the child's innocence.

events.name: Monthly couple financial review and travel fund setup
events.description: After their daughter fell asleep (around 11 o'clock), Yu Xiaowei took out the April spending receipts from her handbag, and her husband Zhang Weiming brought out the family account book. The two checked the items one by one at the small desk in the study. They focused on reviewing the impulsive purchase of a designer handbag (HK$8,500) and the extra medical expenses for her mother-in-law (about HK$3,000), and confirmed that total spending exceeded the budget by HK$3,000. Based on this, they jointly adjusted the May budget: cut dining out and non-essential shopping by 10%, and increase the monthly emergency reserve from HK$2,000 to HK$3,000. At the same time, Yu Xiaowei proposed setting up an annual family travel fund, with a goal of saving an additional HK$20,000 before the end of the year, depositing a fixed HK$4,000 each month from the surplus into a dedicated savings account starting in May. Zhang Weiming signed in support. Finally, Yu Xiaowei took a photo of the meeting notes for archiving and set a phone reminder to review again next month.

start_state.location: At home on Prince Edward Road West
start_state.mood: A new week begins, psyching myself up for my mother-in-law's recovery plan, but I'm a bit sleepy from going to bed late last night.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Daughter's gift and husband's collaboration plan brought deep comfort; tired but fulfilled inside.

state.daily_exercise: 3 sets of planks, several neck and shoulder stretches, and about 12,000 steps walked throughout the day.

2025-04.daily_overview: Her mother-in-law's follow-up results were encouraging, marking a new stage in her recovery. Yu Xiaowei accompanied her to the follow-up in the morning and arranged a yum cha breakfast to celebrate. In the afternoon, she completed the care handover with her husband. Then she was able to catch her breath, started clearing the work that had been set aside, and planned to return to her normal routine. In the evening, she finally had time to spread out her yoga mat in the living room and did a relatively complete stretching routine, feeling her body gradually waking up. At noon, she opened a Japanese-learning app to memorize 20 words — fragmented study finally began to pay off.

events.name: Accompany mother-in-law to orthopedic follow-up visit
events.description: At 8:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei went to Kwun Tong to pick up her mother-in-law and went to United Christian Hospital for a follow-up visit. After the examination, Dr. Zhou Wenbin confirmed that the ligament had healed well and the swelling had completely subsided. She could gradually resume normal walking, but he recommended one more physical therapy session. Yu Xiaowei asked in detail about precautions for going up and down stairs and scheduled the final physical therapy session.

events.name: Going for morning tea to celebrate recovery
events.description: After the follow-up appointment ended around 10 a.m., Yu Xiaowei took her mother-in-law to a time-honored teahouse in Kwun Tong for yum cha. The two ordered shrimp dumplings, chicken feet, BBQ pork buns, and two bowls of double-steamed milk custard. Her mother-in-law was in high spirits and kept saying how hard Xiaowei had been working lately. Yu Xiaowei smiled and said that once her foot was fully recovered, she would take her to buy new shoes on the weekend.

events.name: Handover of caregiving responsibilities.
events.description: At 1 p.m., Yu Xiaowei organized the week's medication list and key care points into a table, sent it to her husband Zhang Weiming via WeChat, and attached a link to a video on using a walking cane. After staying with her mother-in-law for an afternoon nap, she returned to her own home. She left the keys to her mother-in-law's house with her husband, and they agreed that he would mainly visit after work for the next few days. She also called her mother-in-law's neighbor, Auntie Chan, and asked her to drop by more often during the day; the woman readily agreed.

events.name: Clear the work backlog
events.description: At 3 p.m., back at home on Prince Edward Road West, Yu Xiaowei replied to a week's backlog of work emails one by one, handling a total of 17 unread emails, including 3 renewal reminders, 5 product inquiries, and 2 team notices. She sent client Chen Meiling a follow-up email about the claims progress, copying the company's claims department, and also apologized to client Wang Qiming, agreeing to send the preliminary cross-border group insurance plan before this weekend.

events.name: Evening light workout at home
events.description: At 6 p.m., Yu Xiaowei finally had some free time. She spread out her yoga mat in the living room and followed a mobile app for a 30-minute vinyasa yoga session, focusing on stretching her legs and back, which were tense from days of running around. Her mother, Chen Meiling, was knitting beside her, occasionally glancing at her with a relieved smile.

events.name: Evening family time and future planning
events.description: After dinner, Yu Xiaowei helped her son with his homework and read the picture book Ballet Princess to her daughter. After the children fell asleep, she sat at her desk and planned the priorities for the coming week in her notes: 1. Arrange to talk with her father about investing (weekend); 2. Complete Wang Qiming's proposal; 3. Resume a morning run once; 4. Catch up on the CFP course. She felt that life had become manageable again.

events.name: First attempt at fragmented Japanese learning.
events.description: During the lunch break, while waiting for her mother-in-law to take a nap, Yu Xiaowei took out her phone and used the Duolingo app to learn 20 Japanese kana and basic greetings, and completed a speaking practice session. She took a screenshot and sent it to the CFP study group to share her micro-learning method, and the group members all gave it likes.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Knowing that today was the follow-up appointment, she felt anticipation inside.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Felt relaxed and optimistic because of her mother-in-law's recovery and life getting back on track

state.daily_exercise: 30 minutes of yoga in the evening, and 5 minutes of standing stretches during the lunch break.

2025-04.daily_overview: Life gradually returned to normal. Yu Xiaowei worked efficiently in the Wan Chai office all day, focusing on the draft cross-border group insurance plan, customer claims follow-up, and the team's quarterly data summary. During the lunch break, she went out to lunch with Su Lishan, and the rare casual chat with a colleague relieved the high pressure. In the early morning, she boldly tried a recovery jog. Although her pace was slow, she felt invigorated after sweating profusely. Before bed, she formally sent her father an invitation to have a detailed talk over the weekend and began to consider how to express it gently.

events.name: Attempting a recovery jog in the early morning
events.description: At 6 a.m., Yu Xiaowei put on her running shoes and jogged along Prince Edward Road West to the nearby Kowloon Tsai Park, running 3 kilometers at a pace of 7:30 per kilometer. It was her first outdoor run in two weeks, and she found her cardio somewhat challenging, but the sweat refreshed her. After the run, she stretched thoroughly for 10 minutes, and the discomfort in her neck almost disappeared. After returning home, she made breakfast and sent the children to school.

events.name: Focusing on cross-border plans at the office
events.description: From 9 a.m. to noon, Yu Xiaowei focused on drafting a cross-border group medical insurance plan for client Wang Qiming in her office. She referred to the rate table of the company's Shenzhen branch and called her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng in Shenzhen to consult on the integration of mainland employees' social insurance. After completing the first draft, she sent it to her actuarial colleague Guo Junwei for professional opinions.

events.name: Lunch break meal with Su Lishan
events.description: At 12:30 pm, colleague Su Lishan took Yu Xiaowei to a newly opened Vietnamese restaurant near the company for pho. Su Lishan shared her experience of just signing a small business owner client, and asked about the recovery of Yu Xiaowei's mother-in-law. The two agreed to sign up for an evening yoga class near the company together once her mother-in-law fully recovered. After the meal, they took a 15-minute walk nearby and talked about possible future changes in the team. Su Lishan hinted that they should pay more attention to cross-border business.

events.name: Follow up on client Chen Meiling's claim.
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei contacted the company's claims department to expedite Ms. Chen Meiling's hospitalization medical claim. Upon learning that it was delayed due to difficulties in retrieving medical records from the Social Welfare Department, she immediately called Chen Meiling to explain, and proactively offered a free family policy review service as an apology. The client's attitude softened and she expressed understanding.

events.name: Organize team quarterly data
events.description: At 4 p.m., her superior Liang Zhenhua asked Yu Xiaowei to compile the team’s premium income and policy count for this quarter for next week’s regional meeting. She spent nearly two hours exporting data from the system and making simple charts. She found that the share of potential cross-border business had risen to 15%, highlighted this as a bright spot, and planned to propose setting up a cross-border business team at the meeting.

events.name: Evening supermarket shopping and family dinner
events.description: After work, Yu Xiaowei stopped by the Kowloon City market on the way home and bought fresh prawns and vegetables. After returning home, she cooked, making garlic steamed prawns and blanched choy sum, while her mother Chen Meiling made scallion pancakes. It was a rare occasion for the family to eat in rather than eating out, and the children enjoyed the food with relish.

events.name: Before bed, formally invited her father to talk this weekend.
events.description: At 9 p.m., after careful consideration in her study, Yu Xiaowei sent a voice WeChat message to her father Yu Guoqiang. In a gentle but clear tone, she said: “Dad, I've done some research on that wealth management project. There are some things I'd like to discuss with you in detail over the weekend. How about I come to you for tea on Saturday morning? Let's have Mom join us too.” Her father quickly replied, “Okay.” Only then did she feel somewhat at ease. After going to bed, she still read articles on preventing financial fraud.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Determined to return to regular exercise; struggled a bit when getting up early but felt full of anticipation.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.

2025-04.daily_overview: On a workday, Yu Xiaowei turned her attention to long-term planning and learning. The external training in the morning broadened her perspective on tax issues for high-net-worth clients; during the lunch break she spoke with Guo Junwei on the phone about scheme details; in the afternoon she produced an optimized version of the cross-border plan. In the early evening she resumed her morning yoga practice, and in the evening she systematically caught up with the CFP online course and kept a learning log. A sense of order was gradually being rebuilt. She also browsed autumn marathon event information during the lunch break, quietly planting a new goal in her mind.

events.name: Attended the company's tax-themed training in the morning.
events.description: At 9 a.m., Yu Xiaowei attended a three-hour lecture on insurance and tax planning for high-net-worth clients, given by an external tax advisor, in the meeting room at the Wan Chai headquarters. She took detailed notes on income tax and estate tax points involving Hong Kong and mainland China tax residents in cross-border insurance policies, accumulating knowledge for serving clients like Wang Qiming.

events.name: During the lunch break, consulted Guo Junwei and refined the proposal.
events.description: At 12:30 pm, Yu Xiaowei had a video call in the company rest area with her Guangzhou colleague Guo Junwei to discuss details about the coverage of the direct payment network for mainland Class 3A hospitals in the cross-border group medical plan. Based on Guo's suggestion, she adjusted part of the hospital list in the plan and added a green-channel clause for outpatient appointments. After the lunch break, she sent the revised version to Wang Qiming, attaching a WeChat voice message explaining the key optimizations. After the call, she stood by the window and did a few minutes of shoulder relaxation exercises.

events.name: Handling her mother-in-law's final physical therapy appointment
events.description: At 3 p.m., Yu Xiaowei took time to call the community physiotherapy centre and booked her mother-in-law's final treatment for next Wednesday (April 30), confirming that her husband Zhang Weiming could accompany her then. She told her husband in the family group chat and uploaded a photo of the appointment slip.

events.name: Evening regular yoga class
events.description: At 6 p.m., Yu Xiaowei left work one hour early (compensatory time off), returned home, changed into yoga clothes, and followed a YouTuber through a 45-minute Hatha yoga session focused on strengthening the core and hips. Her mother Chen Meiling did simple movements alongside her, and the mother and daughter kept laughing at each other's awkward poses.

events.name: Evening CFP online course catch-up and note organization
events.description: At 8 p.m., after the children fell asleep, Yu Xiaowei opened the CFP basic course online platform in her study and focused on two lessons in the personal tax planning module, totaling 1.5 hours. She wrote down key formulas and key takeaways in her notebook and set herself three calculation questions. She planned to complete another mock test this weekend.

events.name: Bedtime meditation and study review
events.description: At 10:15 p.m., after finishing the online course, Yu Xiaowei sat cross-legged on the living room rug and did 10 minutes of mindfulness meditation, focusing on her breathing. Then she wrote in her diary: "Studied 3.5 hours today; I feel CFP is turning from a burden into confidence." She fell asleep with a sense of satisfaction.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: After yesterday's reset, my spirits are a bit lifted today; I want to try to have an efficient day.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: The sense of progress from learning eased her recent anxiety, and she felt calm inside.

state.daily_exercise: 45 minutes of Hatha yoga, 5 minutes of shoulder stretching during the lunch break.

2025-04.daily_overview: Her mother-in-law had essentially recovered, and the family caregiving arrangement was officially ended. In the morning, Yu Xiaowei accompanied her mother-in-law to the last follow-up visit, which confirmed the ligament had healed. At noon, the family had a symbolic celebratory lunch together. In the afternoon, she returned to the office and urgently handled a sudden claims dispute from a high-end client, showing professionalism. In the evening, she finally had time to take the kids to the night market, and bought a gift to give her father during the weekend talk — an introduction to a formal retirement wealth management product, which she planned to use as a bridge for communication. While shopping, she also picked out a new pair of running shoes for herself as a reward for getting back into training.

events.name: Accompany her mother-in-law to the final follow-up appointment.
events.description: At 9 a.m., Yu Xiaowei took a half day off and, together with her husband Zhang Weiming, accompanied her mother-in-law to Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital to see Dr. Zhou Wenbin. After an ultrasound examination, the doctor announced that the ligament had healed and she could walk with full weight-bearing, but she must avoid strenuous exercise for one month. Her mother-in-law was so happy that she immediately called her old friends to share the good news.

events.name: Family celebration lunch
events.description: After leaving the hospital, Yu Xiaowei suggested celebrating with lunch at a Teochew restaurant in Kwun Tong. She ordered a braised platter, oyster omelette, and stir-fried seasonal vegetables. Her mother-in-law had a good appetite. After the meal, Yu Xiaowei said to her mother-in-law in a serious tone, "From now on, ask Weiming to help with mopping and lifting things. Don't try to handle it on your own anymore." Her mother-in-law smiled and agreed.

events.name: Took herself off the caregiving rotation and thanked the neighbor.
events.description: At 1 p.m., Yu Xiaowei bought a fruit basket at the fruit shop downstairs from her mother-in-law's house and delivered it specifically to the neighbor Mrs. He's home, to thank her for looking after them over the past few days. Mrs. He declined repeatedly but finally accepted, saying more than once that neighbors don't need to be so polite. Only then did Yu Xiaowei leave at ease and head straight to the company.

events.name: Handled an unexpected customer claims dispute in the afternoon.
events.description: At 3 p.m., after arriving at the office, Yu Xiaowei saw that a high-end client, Mr. Li, whose claim for an accidental fall injury had been rejected, was complaining on the phone to her supervisor Liang Zhenhua. She immediately took over the call, listened calmly, and checked the policy terms, discovering that the claim had been rejected because the client had not reported the incident within 24 hours. She explained this sincerely to the client, and at the same time proactively contacted the claims department to seek an ex gratia payment, promising a reply within two days. Liang Zhenhua acknowledged her handling of the crisis.

events.name: Left work early and took the children to the Kowloon City night market.
events.description: At 6 p.m., Yu Xiaowei left work on time, went home to pick up the two excited children, and went with her mother Chen Meiling to the weekend night market near Kowloon City Market. They ate waffles and bought small toys. Her daughter Yuxin stood at a handicraft stall for a long time looking at embroidered handkerchiefs. Yu Xiaowei thought to herself that she could teach her Cantonese embroidery in the future. The night market trip temporarily made her forget the daytime dispute.

events.name: Prepare communication materials for father and reward myself.
events.description: At 9 p.m., after the children were asleep, Yu Xiaowei used her computer in the study to organize several pages of materials on identifying financial fraud, and downloaded introductions to two low-risk bond funds from the bank's official website. She planned that when she talked to her father the next day, she would listen first, then analyze objectively from a caring perspective, and finally present legitimate products as alternatives. After putting the materials into a folder, she opened the shopping app on her phone and ordered a pair of professional cushioned running shoes as a reward for returning to training, looking forward to trying them on next week.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Friday's relaxation was interwoven with the tension of the upcoming conversation with her father.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Felt at ease after being fully prepared for tomorrow, and enjoyed brief family joy and a little self-reward.

state.daily_exercise: A lot of walking, about 10,000 steps.

2025-04.daily_overview: The morning was a warm mother-daughter art day. The ballet girl and butterflies in her daughter's painting unexpectedly triggered Yu Xiaowei's inspiration for Cantonese embroidery. She quickly sketched the 'Butterfly Dance' series, but hesitated and didn't let herself fully immerse in it. After returning home in the afternoon, she had a key conversation alone with her father at a cha chaan teng. In a gentle but firm way, she successfully persuaded him to give up the high-risk project and helped him open a prudent wealth-management account. With a heavy weight lifted, the whole family went to her mother-in-law's home for a reunion dinner in a harmonious atmosphere. She also called her best friend Lin Jiaxin during a break at the art festival, sharing the joy of her daughter's painting, and they agreed to meet after Mother's Day.

events.name: Participate in the kindergarten’s “Spring Art Festival”
events.description: At 9 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei changed into a white cotton-linen top and wide-leg pants and took her daughter Zhang Yuxin to Kowloon City Baptist Church Kindergarten. The campus was decorated with balloons and ribbons, and the first activity they attended was parent-child watercolor painting. Xinxin painted a girl in a pink ballet tulle skirt standing in a flower garden, surrounded by seven colorful butterflies. Yu Xiaowei crouched beside her, watching her focused profile, her heart full of motherly affection.

events.name: A surge of inspiration for creating Cantonese embroidery.
events.description: During the free creation session at 10:30, Yu Xiaowei looked at her daughter's painting and suddenly recalled Teacher Wu Xiuying's concept of using embroidery thread to express light and shadow. She immediately took out her portable sketchbook from her bag and quickly sketched a series of drawings themed around butterflies and dancers, along with a few lines of color scheme ideas. But thinking about her recent busy schedule, she did not develop it further. She sighed softly, closed the book, and planned to contact Teacher Wu after her father's matters were resolved.

events.name: Returned home happily with her daughter after the art festival.
events.description: At 11:30 a.m. the event ended. Yu Xiaowei helped her daughter pack up her paintings and handmade clay works, and the two walked hand in hand to a nearby cha chaan teng, bought egg tarts and iced lemon tea, and then went home. Xinxin chattered all the way, and Yu Xiaowei listened with a smile, temporarily forgetting her worries. On the way home, she called Lin Jiaxin and excitedly described her daughter's creations. Lin Jiaxin laughed and said, 'In the future she can be your Guangdong embroidery model.'

events.name: The key conversation with her father
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei returned alone to her parents' home in Kowloon City and chatted with her father Yu Guoqiang at the cha chaan teng downstairs. She first honestly shared her findings on the high-risk project, then patiently explained the common signs of a Ponzi scheme and took out a fraud-prevention article she had prepared in advance. When her father looked gloomy, she pulled out information on two low-risk bank funds and suggested that he split his retirement money into two parts—one for steady allocation at the bank, and the other for flexible daily use. After more than an hour of conversation, her father finally relented and said, "You're really thoughtful, Dad will listen to you." Yu Xiaowei felt relieved, and the father and daughter immediately agreed to go to the bank together next Monday.

events.name: Evening reunion dinner at the mother-in-law's house
events.description: At 6 p.m., Yu Xiaowei's family of four plus her parents gathered at her mother-in-law's home in Kwun Tong. Zhang Weiming cooked his signature steamed pork ribs with black bean sauce, and her mother-in-law contributed winter melon and barley old duck soup that had been simmered all afternoon. At the dinner table, Yu Xiaowei announced that her father's finances had been properly resolved, her mother-in-law had recovered, and the cat had come home. The whole family raised their cups of tea to celebrate. The children performed a new song they had learned in kindergarten, and laughter filled the room.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home on Prince Edward Road West.
start_state.mood: Looking forward to parent-child time, but also a little nervous about the afternoon conversation.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home on Prince Edward Road West.
end_state.mood: The successful resolution of her father's matter brought great relief, leaving her refreshed in both mind and body.

state.daily_exercise: No dedicated exercise, but moderate activity throughout the day, with 2 sets of scattered squats.

2025-04.daily_overview: On Sunday, Yu Xiaowei took an important step toward resuming running. In the early morning, she went alone to Kowloon Tsai Park and completed a 3 km jog at a controlled pace of 7:15 per kilometer. Though out of breath, she was full of joy. Afterwards, she returned home and took the whole family to the park to enjoy the sunshine. In the afternoon she did housework, went out for dinner in the evening, and in the late evening planned her May study schedule and Cantonese embroidery while preparing to return to work and training the following week. She shared her morning-running photos in the CFP study group; friends all encouraged her, and running buddy Shen Peiwen also sent congratulations, agreeing to formally resume Wednesday night runs in May.

events.name: Early morning recovery jog
events.description: At 6:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei quietly got up, changed into the new cushioned running shoes she bought last night, and slipped out of the house. She went alone to Kowloon Tsai Park and jogged 3 kilometers in loops at a pace of about 7:15 per kilometer. It was her first outdoor long run in nearly half a month. Her heart rate was slightly high, but her breathing gradually became steady, and sweat carried away days of stress. After the run, she stretched carefully for 10 minutes, took a selfie in the morning light, and posted it to the CFP study group with the caption: “Restart step one: an easy 3 km run.” After returning home and showering, she felt refreshed.

events.name: Morning parent-child time at the park
events.description: At 9 a.m., Yu Xiaowei took her daughter Zhang Yuxin and son Zhang Zixuan to Kowloon Tsai Park again. Xinxin, wearing a pink ballet tulle skirt, twirled and jumped on the grass, and she took many photos with her phone. Her son played football with his dad. The sunlight was just right; Yu Xiaowei sat on a bench watching her family and felt a rare sense of peace.

events.name: Inquiring about summer swimming classes for her son.
events.description: After the morning park activities, Yu Xiaowei stopped by the swimming centre at the Kowloon City District Sports Centre to ask about summer children's swimming courses. She chose an eight-week beginner class for her son, held Tuesday and Thursday mornings, and enrolled and paid on the spot. She hopes her son will gain an extra sports skill outside of school.

events.name: Video call with her best friend Lin Jiaxin at noon
events.description: While eating lunch at home, Yu Xiaowei chatted with her best friend Lin Jiaxin over a video call. Lin Jiaxin mentioned that the school has a parent-child sports day next month and she was worrying about what props to prepare. Yu Xiaowei suggested making the class sign with Cantonese embroidery. Lin Jiaxin laughed and said it was too exquisite, but still encouraged her to take up embroidery again. The two agreed to meet around Mother's Day.

events.name: Afternoon housework and seasonal storage organization.
events.description: At 1 p.m., Yu Xiaowei kicked off a family deep cleaning. She packed the thick winter comforters and sweaters into vacuum bags and placed them on the top shelf of the storage cabinet, then hung out the light spring jackets and skirts. Her husband Zhang Weiming was responsible for cleaning the air conditioner filters and fans. The children helped by passing hangers on the side, and although they were more of a hindrance than a help, the atmosphere was cheerful. While tidying up, she repeatedly squatted, stood up, and stretched, treating it as light exercise.

events.name: The whole family went out for dinner in the evening
events.description: At 5:30 in the evening, Yu Xiaowei suggested not cooking at home, and the family of five (including her mother Chen Meiling) walked to a conveyor-belt sushi restaurant in Kowloon City for dinner. The children excitedly took plates from the conveyor belt, and Yu Xiaowei specially picked out the tamago sushi her daughter loved and the grilled salmon her husband liked. The meal cost 320 Hong Kong dollars in total, and everyone felt this Sunday was very pleasant.

events.name: Planning CFP study and Cantonese embroidery in the evening
events.description: At 8:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowei put up a new monthly calendar on the study wall, highlighted the key module dates for the May CFP course with a highlighter, and planned to focus on studying every Tuesday and Thursday evening. She also listed in her notebook the materials needed for the “Butterfly Dance” Cantonese embroidery: silk base fabric, gradient silk thread, No. 12 embroidery needles, etc., intending to place an order with Ms. Wu Xiuying before the end of the month and book a studio visit for advice. Before bed, she agreed with her running buddy Shen Peiwen on WeChat that the first Wednesday evening run in May would officially resume. Shen Peiwen replied, “Waiting for you!”

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Early Sunday morning, with an eagerness to resume running.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: The dual fulfillment of family day and restarting running, full of anticipation for May.

state.daily_exercise: Morning 3 km run (pace 7:15/km), 10 minutes of stretching, household chores

2025-04.daily_overview: On Monday, Yu Xiaowei officially resumed all regular arrangements: her daughter's ballet class restarted, and she personally handled the drop-offs and pickups; at work, she smoothly initiated the finalization of Wang Qiming's cross-border plan; in the evening, she and her husband agreed to move her CFP study time to the early morning, and gained her husband's support in studying alongside her. Life was fully back on track, and there was even a new momentum of working side by side. Her colleague Su Lishan sent a card congratulating her mother-in-law on her recovery, which warmed Yu Xiaowei's heart.

events.name: Morning CFP study and household division of labor adjustment
events.description: At 5 a.m., Yu Xiaowei got up quietly, took her coffee to the study, and began trying out her new early-morning study plan. She reviewed two chapters on tax-saving planning and completed the exercises. After studying until 7, she woke the children and discussed with her husband that he would handle the children's breakfast and school drop-off today, while she would simply prepare her daughter's ballet items for the afternoon. Though sleepy, her focus was higher than at night.

events.name: Daughter's ballet class resumed, and she personally handles drop-off and pick-up.
events.description: At 4 p.m., Yu Xiaowei left work half an hour early, drove from Wan Chai back to Kowloon City, and picked up her daughter Zhang Yuxin, who was wearing a new tulle skirt, from Wuyue Ballet Studio. Xinxin excitedly showed off the new small jump combination the teacher had taught, and Yu Xiaowei praised her for improving quickly. She then paid next month's tuition to the teacher in charge, Ms. Zhu, and thanked her for the video homework guidance during the earlier class suspension. While waiting, she did several sets of wall sits in the hallway.

events.name: Work: completed and finalized the cross-border plan, then sent it.
events.description: In the morning at the office, Yu Xiaowei, based on Guo Junwei's email feedback over the weekend, fine-tuned the details of the list of designated hospitals on the mainland in Wang Qiming's cross-border group insurance plan and added an emergency medical evacuation clause. After finalizing it, she sent it to Wang Qiming by formal email, copied her supervisor Liang Zhenhua, and left a WeChat message saying she would arrange a video call to explain it whenever Manager Wang was free.

events.name: Handle other clients' policy renewals and inquiries.
events.description: That day she also efficiently answered 5 client calls, including reminding her old classmate He Junjie that his auto insurance expires next week and to renew it in time. He Junjie also mentioned the class reunion. She promised to organize a small get-together once she was less busy.

events.name: Evening family meeting confirms the new daily schedule.
events.description: After dinner, Yu Xiaowei had a detailed discussion with her husband Zhang Weiming in the living room, confirming that starting May 1, she would get up at 5 a.m. every day to study CFP until 7 a.m. Her husband was willing to get up at the same time to prepare a glass of warm water for her and sit beside her reading, accompanying her in his own way. Zhang Weiming also offered to help her organize her mistake notebook once a week. Yu Xiaowei was deeply moved and held his hand tightly.

events.name: Gratitude before bed and preparation for the next day
events.description: At 10 p.m., after washing up, Yu Xiaowei wrote in her phone memo: “Today I resumed ballet drop-offs and pickups, work progressed smoothly, and Weiming promised to get up early with me—life is really getting better.” She put on a soothing eye mask and soon fell asleep.

events.name: A heartwarming card from colleague Su Lishan
events.description: When she returned to the office at noon, Yu Xiaowei found a handwritten card on her desk that Su Lishan had quietly placed there. On it was a cartoon orange cat and a few small flowers, with the message: "Congratulations on your mother-in-law's recovery & the cat coming home, Awei, keep going!" Touched, she took a photo and sent it to the family group chat. Her husband replied with a smiling emoji.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Slightly drowsy from carrying out the new daily routine, but full of determination.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Moved by her husband’s support and colleagues’ thoughtfulness, and reassured by the pace of recovery.

state.daily_exercise: Wall sits, 3 sets; stretching in spare moments while picking up/dropping off my daughter.

2025-04.daily_overview: Three generations of the family gathered at a long-established teahouse in Kowloon City to celebrate the mother-in-law's recovery and the resolution of the father's financial problems with a hearty dim sum breakfast. Laughter filled the meal as the children chattered about funny school stories, and the adults thanked one another—family cohesion reached a recent high. After dim sum, Yu Xiaowei took her parents to browse the street market. In the afternoon she returned to the office to finish part of her work, and in the evening she paid a brief visit to Teacher Wu Xiuying's studio to formally announce that she would launch the Butterfly Dance series. Her life returned to a reassuring routine. She realized that getting up at 5 a.m. to study was too tiring, so she decided to adjust her schedule starting tomorrow and get up at 6 a.m., prioritizing sleep.

events.name: Early-morning study and departure preparation
events.description: At 5 a.m., Yu Xiaowei dragged herself out of bed. After reading half an hour of the CFP risk management chapter, she felt obviously drowsy and inefficient. She decided this would be her last attempt at such an early schedule and that she needed to seriously reflect on her study pace during the day. At 6:30, she woke up the whole family, changed the children into neat shirts and skirts, helped her mother Chen Meiling choose a patterned xiangyunsha top, and urged her husband Zhang Weiming to go get the car early.

events.name: Family morning tea to celebrate recovery and reconciliation.
events.description: At 8:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei's family, including her parents and mother-in-law, gathered at the Dimao Guan Teahouse in Kowloon City. She had booked a large table by the window a week earlier. Dim sum arrived one after another: shrimp dumplings, siu mai, barbecue pork buns, fresh bean curd rolls, steamed ribs... Her mother-in-law Li Shufen was the first to stand up, toasting with tea instead of wine to thank her daughter-in-law and son for their care. Yu Guoqiang also took the initiative to say that he had almost done something foolish and that his daughter had stopped him. Yu Xiaowei's eyes turned slightly red, and she raised her glass, saying that the most important thing for a family is to be together. The children competed over who ate more shrimp dumplings, and the atmosphere was warm and lively.

events.name: Accompanying my parents to the street market and choosing fabric for my mother
events.description: After morning tea, at around 10:30, Yu Xiaowei had her husband take her mother-in-law and the children home first, while she accompanied her parents to the fabric market downstairs. Her mother, Chen Meiling, took a fancy to a piece of pale blue-green cotton-linen and wanted to make a qipao for her granddaughter. Yu Xiaowei paid for it without hesitation and suggested embroidering a few small flowers on the cuffs. Her mother smiled and said she would let Yu Xiaowei do the embroidery once she graduated from her Cantonese embroidery apprenticeship. Her father, meanwhile, picked out a few taels of fish maw at the dried goods stall, saying it was to nourish her mother-in-law.

events.name: Return to the company in the afternoon to handle backlogged matters.
events.description: At 12:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowei rushed to the office in Wan Chai and used her lunch break to handle the internal reports that had piled up last week, and prepared a short PPT on the feasibility of a cross-border business team for Wednesday’s regional meeting. She also contacted the bank relationship manager Li Guodong to consult about corporate group insurance cooperation and lead generation, and made an appointment for a detailed discussion after the holiday.

events.name: Visited Teacher Wu Xiuying to launch the Butterfly Dance series.
events.description: At 4 p.m., Yu Xiaowei left work early, carrying gift tea, and went to Teacher Wu Xiuying's studio in Sham Shui Po. She showed the teacher her daughter's painting and her own sketches. Teacher Wu's eyes lit up, praised the natural inspiration, and immediately helped her match sheer silk and extremely fine silver thread suitable for expressing the translucent quality of butterfly wings, suggesting combining long-and-short stitch with stem stitch. The two agreed that starting next month, she would come every Sunday afternoon to learn and improve. A small weight concerning her hobby quietly lifted in Yu Xiaowei's heart.

events.name: Evening family video call and reflection on daily routine
events.description: At 9 p.m., Yu Xiaowei had a video call with her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng in the living room, told him that their father's matter had been properly resolved, and chatted about work in Shenzhen and recent updates. Afterwards, she and her husband quickly went through next week's calendar, and she admitted that getting up early to study for several consecutive days had made her drowsy during the day and actually reduced her efficiency. She decided to adjust her wake-up time to 6:30 starting tomorrow and extend her evening study time by one hour. Zhang Weiming supported this. She felt this adjustment was more sustainable.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Excited about dim sum day, she woke up early, but her sleepiness was hard to hide.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: The dual joy of family cohesion and restarting personal hobbies; a sense of inner fulfillment, and she adjusted her daily routine with ease.

state.daily_exercise: Walked around the street market, about 8,000 steps; no dedicated exercise.

2025-04.daily_overview: On the last day of April, Yu Xiaowei received recognition at the morning regional meeting for her cross-border business proposal; at noon she accompanied her mother-in-law to complete the final physical therapy session, officially marking the end of the family health crisis; in the afternoon she returned to the office, finished routine matters, then went home early and made wontons with the children. In the evening, amid a thunderstorm, she reviewed the month's high pressure and gains, wrote a long monthly summary, and adjusted her plan for the next month: making morning yoga and meditation a daily ritual, keeping fragmented training, moving CFP study to the evening, and resuming long-distance running on weekends. She also shared her time management insights from the family crisis in the CFP group, and confirmed with her running partner Shen Peiwen that they would resume night running on May 7. Before bed, she did 20 minutes of meditation, settling her mind from the noise and infusing May with determination and calm.

events.name: Morning yoga and meditation
events.description: At 6:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei woke up to her alarm. Following her new plan, she no longer studied in the early morning; instead, she went to the living room and unrolled her yoga mat. She followed an online video for 10 minutes of vinyasa yoga, focusing on stretching her hips, neck, and shoulders, then sat cross-legged for 5 minutes of mindfulness meditation, concentrating on her breath to set a calm tone for the day. She felt that the discomfort in her neck had completely disappeared.

events.name: Monthly regional business meeting.
events.description: At 9 a.m., Yu Xiaowei attended the regional sales meeting chaired by Liang Zhenhua. She reported the performance data of her client segment and formally proposed establishing a dedicated cross-border business team, noting that customer resources in Shenzhen and Hong Kong could be integrated. Liang Zhenhua expressed approval and asked her to submit a detailed feasibility plan before the end of Q2, hinting that team headcount might be expanded if progress went smoothly. She felt greatly encouraged.

events.name: At noon, accompany my mother-in-law to complete her last physical therapy session.
events.description: After the meeting, Yu Xiaowei rushed to Kwun Tong during her lunch break to accompany her mother-in-law to the community center for her final physical therapy session. The therapist spoke highly of her mother-in-law's recovery and gave suggestions for the next stage of self-training. Yu Xiaowei recorded a video and thanked the therapist. When they walked out of the center, her mother-in-law said she could now walk without a cane. Yu Xiaowei held her arm as they walked slowly, feeling the sunlight especially warm. While waiting during therapy, she did 3 sets of wall sits and 2 sets of bird dogs in the corridor to maintain her fragmented training habit.

events.name: Returned to the office in the afternoon to handle routine work
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei returned to the office, processed payroll verification and expense reimbursements, and assigned the new team member He Junwen (a recently hired assistant) the task of organizing the client birthday list. She also called her mother, Chen Meiling, to check the inventory in the refrigerator and discuss making wontons together in the evening. Colleague Su Lishan came by for a chat, and the two exchanged tips on balancing family and work, encouraging each other.

events.name: Left work early for parent-child wonton making
events.description: At 5 p.m., Yu Xiaowei left work on time and went home. She minced fresh shrimp, pork, and black fungus, then mixed the filling with her mother. She called the two kids to wash their hands and learn to wrap wontons. Her daughter Yuxin's wontons were crooked, while her son Zixuan insisted on putting too much filling, resulting in several bursting open. The whole family laughed together. This simple everyday warmth made Yu Xiaowei feel deeply grateful.

events.name: April review and May plan
events.description: At 8 p.m., while the children watched cartoons in the living room, Yu Xiaowei sat in the study and opened her diary to review the entire month of April in detail. She listed positive events: 'mother-in-law's recovery, the settlement of father's investment troubles, the cat's return, daughter's painting, new financial rules for the couple, and the launch of the cross-border plan.' She also noted the lessons of 'interrupted Japanese studies, impulse purchases, interrupted long-distance running, and lagging CFP progress.' She paid special attention to the interruption of her Japanese studies and decided to continue self-study during fragmented commuting time starting in May, while adjusting CFP study to a fixed evening slot and no longer forcing herself to get up in the early morning. Based on this, she adjusted her May plan: 1. Morning runs of 5-8 km every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday; 2. Daily 6:30 morning yoga and meditation, with 1.5 hours of CFP study in the evening; 3. Half a day of Cantonese embroidery on weekends; 4. A dinner alone with her husband once a week. She printed out the plan and put it on the refrigerator. Coach Zhao criticized her unstable mindset and said sternly: “If you run like this, how can you finish the street marathon at the end of the month?” He demanded that she strictly follow the planned pace, and gave detailed adjustment suggestions: lower the pace, add core strength training and meditation relaxation. After the training session, she felt frustrated and sat alone on the sideline using a foam roller to relax. Shen Peiwen handed her a bottle of water and said softly, “There are still three weeks, enough time to adjust.”

She held back her anger and disappointment, maintaining her politeness on the surface, though her voice had become somewhat stiff. Her brother realized he had misspoken and tried to change the subject.

She had her husband and children get into the car first, stood at the entrance of the restaurant and took several deep breaths, and only then barely managed to suppress the surging emotions before getting into the car and returning home. Along the way, she did not say a word.

During the conversation, although Yu Xiaowei tried to participate, she was distracted several times and didn't even respond in time when her daughter called her. Zhang Weiming noticed all of this.

events.name: Insomnia late at night; her husband took the initiative to comfort her.
events.description: At 11 p.m., Yu Xiaowei lay in bed tossing and turning, scenes of the client being snatched away and the cold war with her father replaying in her mind. Zhang Weiming had noticed something off about her during dinner, so he got up, went to the kitchen, made two cups of hot milk, sat by the bed, and asked softly: 'Is something wrong? It'll feel better if you talk about it.' Yu Xiaowei finally let down her guard and poured out everything about Zhou Minyi's betrayal and her father's stubborn insistence on investing. Her husband held her hand and said, 'No matter what happens outside, there will always be someone at home who has your back.' The two talked until 2 a.m., and Yu Xiaowei felt a sense of peace she hadn't had in a long time.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Still anxious after waking up early, but decided to fight back with running and action.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: After venting, she felt incredibly light, grateful for her husband's support, and regained her strength.

state.daily_exercise: 6 km easy run, ice therapy after the run

2025-10.daily_overview: On Saturday, Yu Xiaowei and her husband attended a low-calorie cooking workshop, learned healthy cooking, and agreed to create a new dish each month. In the afternoon, she focused on organizing her CFP notes for about 3 hours, then took her daughter and the cat Bailey to the pet clinic for vaccinations. In the evening, the family enjoyed the quinoa rice balls they had made together, feeling warm and happy.

events.name: Morning yoga breathing practice
events.description: At 7 a.m., Yu Xiaowei did 20 minutes of morning yoga and breathing exercises in her Cantonese embroidery-themed yoga space at home. Coordinating with meditation music and focusing on deep breaths, she set a calm tone for the day.

events.name: Attended a community low-calorie cooking workshop with her husband.
events.description: From 9 a.m. to 11 a.m., Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming went to the community activity center in Kowloon City District to attend a low-calorie home cooking workshop led by a nutritionist. The couple worked together to make three dishes: salmon avocado salad, quinoa rice balls, and tofu cheesecake. Her husband was in charge of cutting and preparing ingredients, while she handled seasoning and plating. At the end of the workshop, they agreed to cook one new dish together every month.

events.name: Focused on organizing CFP asset allocation notes.
events.description: From 1 p.m. to 4 p.m., Yu Xiaowei systematically organized the asset allocation principles she had learned this week in her study. She turned off phone notifications, spread out paper textbooks and notes, repeatedly read the text on difficult points such as rebalancing frequency and transaction costs, and hand-drew a mind map in another notebook. During this time, she drank a cup of homemade low-sugar milk tea to refresh herself (she has already reduced sugar as part of her diet control).

events.name: Take daughter and Bailey the cat to the pet clinic for vaccinations
events.description: At 4:15 p.m., Yu Xiaowei and her daughter Zhang Yuxin got ready to take Bailey out: they put a soft cushion in the cat carrier, brought the vaccination record book and some treats. Her daughter hugged the carrier tightly, and she walked to the pet clinic 800 meters away. At the clinic, she described Bailey's recent appetite and energy levels to the veterinarian, Dr. Chen. After a physical exam, the doctor administered the annual core vaccine. She paid about 300 Hong Kong dollars and received a reminder card.

events.name: After returning home, put an Elizabethan collar on the cat, and the daughter took photos and shared them.
events.description: Around 5 p.m., Yu Xiaowei got home and put an Elizabethan collar on Bailey to keep him from licking. Her daughter thought it looked like a small trumpet, took a photo with her phone, and uploaded it to the family group. Family members replied with laughing emojis. She observed Bailey for half an hour and, seeing no abnormalities, fed him normally.

events.name: Tried making quinoa rice balls in the evening, and the kids loved them
events.description: At 7 p.m., Yu Xiaowei and her husband tried making quinoa rice balls in the kitchen using what they had learned in the workshop, adding corn kernels and chicken floss. Their son and daughter tasted them and said they were delicious, and the family enjoyed a healthy dinner.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: After venting last night, I woke up feeling relaxed and looking forward to the weekend activity.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Family interaction brings a strong sense of happiness and greater confidence in dietary control

state.daily_exercise: 20-minute morning yoga

2025-10.daily_overview: On Sunday, Yu Xiaowei did a 22 km LSD training run with Shen Peiwen in the early morning. It was the last long-distance training session before the street marathon on October 26. The pace was slightly slower than usual due to last week's influence, but she completed the goal. In the morning, she organized her CFP notes; in the afternoon, she focused on the initial stage of a new Cantonese embroidery piece and an eye-care routine. After receiving special embroidery thread from an embroidery friend, she talked with He Meiling on the phone. He Meiling suggested organizing a Shenzhen exchange group, which tempted her. She formally started work on Daughter's World: Autumn and spent the whole afternoon with needle and thread, experiencing a long-lost sense of focused peace.

events.name: Early morning LSD long-distance run of 22 kilometers
events.description: At 5:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei met her running partner Shen Peiwen on the waterfront promenade for a 22-kilometer long slow run. This was the last long-distance training session before the street marathon on October 26, and her coach required her to strictly control her pace to build confidence. She deliberately kept her pace at 6:50 per kilometer to avoid repeating last week's mistake. Although she felt tired midway, the two encouraged each other and completed the workout. Shen Peiwen said, "Let's run at this pace on street marathon day." After the run, she took protein powder and iced her knees and ankles, feeling that her endurance had improved.

events.name: In the morning, organized the wrong answers and notes from portfolio management.
events.description: From 9 a.m. to 12 p.m., Yu Xiaowei organized the wrong answers and difficult points in the Portfolio Management chapter in her study. She reviewed rebalancing frequency, transaction costs, and other topics against the online course replay, and hand-copied three typical calculation problems. In the afternoon, she reviewed the MPT formula and drank homemade low-sugar milk tea to refresh herself. After finishing, she felt her knowledge system was clearer.

events.name: Received the special embroidery thread from He Meiling and talked on the phone
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei received a package from Shenzhen. When she opened it, she found pearlescent silk and gradient silk threads gifted by He Meiling. She excitedly checked the colors and textures, then sorted and stored them in her craft material cabinet. She immediately called He Meiling on WeChat to thank her. He Meiling mentioned that white-collar workers in Shenzhen are increasingly interested in Cantonese embroidery and proposed organizing a small exchange group to come to Hong Kong for a hands-on experience. Yu Xiaowei noted the key points and said she would discuss it with Teacher Wu Xiuying.

events.name: Officially started the creation of Cantonese embroidery piece Daughter's World · Autumn
events.description: From 2:30 to 5:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowei spread white satin on the embroidery frame in the living room and outlined an autumn-themed design with a water-soluble pen: ginkgo leaves, chrysanthemums, and the back view of a little girl. She picked out gold and brown tones from the newly arrived embroidery threads and began her first stitches. She was focused and serene, occasionally looking up to listen to the birds outside the window, feeling joyful.

events.name: Eye care routine and status assessment
events.description: At 7 pm, before cooking, Yu Xiaowei carried out her third weekend eye-care assessment: she used a steam eye mask for 10 minutes to test eye fatigue. She found that her eyes no longer felt dry when looking at her phone screen, and her sleep quality had also improved, confirming that the eye-care habit had become a stable part of her life.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Sunday, mood steady, looking forward to a long-distance run and creative work.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Completed the running goal, gained spiritual fulfillment from Cantonese embroidery, and felt inspired by the exchange group proposal.

state.daily_exercise: 22 km LSD run, followed by icing
