2025-10.daily_overview: On Monday, a workday, Yu Xiaowei completed her interval running training in the early morning. Although she reduced the number of sets to 8 due to fatigue, her pace was acceptable. On her commute, she reviewed CFP knowledge points with flashcards. After arriving at the office, she had a regular meeting with the team, revised the incentive plan based on feedback, and followed up on email replies from some Shenzhen clients. The overall work pace was intense, and during the lunch break she exchanged beauty and skincare tips with Su Lishan.

events.name: Early-morning interval running workout
events.description: At 5:45 a.m., Yu Xiaowei went to Kowloon Tsai Park for interval running: 400 m x 8 sets, with 200 m jog recovery between sets, target pace 4:50/km. She felt heavy in the legs and was noticeably exhausted after the 7th set, but she persisted and completed it. After the run, she stretched thoroughly and used a massage gun to relax. She reported her training to her coach Zhao Zhiming via WeChat, and he replied that it was understandable and suggested adding core training.

events.name: Reviewing core knowledge points with flashcards during the commute
events.description: Leaving home at 7:10 a.m., Yu Xiaowei used the flashcard feature of the CFP study app on the MTR to review asset allocation steps, portfolio construction processes, the efficient frontier, and other topics. She flipped through the cards, silently reciting key terms and repeating the portfolio management framework in her mind. She completed a full review before arriving at the office.

events.name: Weekly team meeting and incentive plan revisions
events.description: At 9:30 a.m., during the weekly team meeting, Director Liang Zhenhua asked Yu Xiaowei to submit the final draft of the Q4 Team Incentive and Work Allocation Optimization Proposal before the end of the day, based on last week's team feedback. At the meeting, she also shared her actions in organizing the Shenzhen client list, which won Liang Zhenhua's approval. He reminded her to also take care of local Hong Kong clients.

events.name: During lunch break, exchanged beauty tips with colleague Su Lishan.
events.description: During lunch break, Yu Xiaowei and Su Lishan had lunch at a nearby cha chaan teng. Su Lishan shared her recent experience with skin booster treatment. Yu Xiaowei was tempted but said she would finish the marathon first before considering it. The two agreed to do radiofrequency treatment together at the end of the month.

events.name: Follow up on the Shenzhen client's email reply.
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei checked her work email and found that among the 20 emails, 5 clients had replied showing interest, 2 of whom scheduled phone calls for Wednesday and Thursday. She organized the relevant contact information into the client follow-up table and felt that her efforts had received initial responses.

events.name: Revise the final draft of the incentive plan and submit it.
events.description: At 4 PM, Yu Xiaowei incorporated the morning's feedback by adding a team collaboration points mechanism to the incentive plan and clearly showed the workflow with charts. Before leaving work, she emailed the final draft to Liang Zhenhua and the entire team, and suggested launching the first pilot run this Friday.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Monday, focused, ready to dive into work and training

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Work is progressing smoothly, and there has been an initial response to the client recovery effort. Despite training fatigue, I feel somewhat relieved.

state.daily_exercise: Interval run: 400m x 8 sets; massage gun relaxation.

2025-10.daily_overview: On Tuesday, Yu Xiaowei spent the day busy with intense work. In the early morning, she attended an Ashtanga morning class but left midway due to fatigue and switched to self-stretching. She used her commute and lunch break to complete CFP practice exercises. In the evening, she received a video call from her close friend Huang Wenhui, who was in Shenzhen. Huang Wenhui gave a rational analysis and shared her own experiences, which significantly improved Yu Xiaowei's mood. After the call, she wrote in her diary and decided to refocus.

events.name: Community Ashtanga morning class (partially attended)
events.description: At 6:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei attended the Ashtanga morning class at the community yoga center, but after 20 minutes she felt unusually tired and could not keep up with the pace, so she signaled to the teacher and left, doing simple stretches in the corner for 5 minutes. She realized that fatigue had accumulated and needed adjustment.

events.name: Handled client consultations and documents during the day
events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowei answered three customer consultation calls at the office and prepared supplementary medical underwriting documents for an insured client. In between, she took the time to contact the bank account manager Li Guodong, mentioned that there might be a need for family estate planning in the future, and agreed to discuss it in detail in November.

events.name: Completed CFP exercises during the commute and lunch break.
events.description: During her commute to and from work and lunch break, Yu Xiaowei completed a total of 30 after-class exercises for the CFP investment planning module on her phone. On the subway, she answered each question and read the explanations, immediately reviewing the textbook for wrong choices. At noon, in the rest area, she wrote her reflections on the practice questions into a notebook and summarized two types of questions that were easy to get wrong.

events.name: Lin Jiaxin contacted Huang Wenhui to ask for help.
events.description: During the day, her best friend Lin Jiaxin, who is in Hong Kong, contacted Huang Wenhui in Shenzhen via WeChat voice message, telling her that Yu Xiaowei had been feeling down lately and hoping that Huang Wenhui could comfort her. Huang Wenhui agreed to have a video call in the evening.

events.name: Video comfort and rational guidance from Huang Wenhui
events.description: At 8 p.m., Huang Wenhui video-called Yu Xiaowei from her home in Shenzhen. She first asked with concern how Xiaowei was doing, then rationally analyzed: 'Zhou Minyi stealing clients is a character issue. Rather than draining yourself, you should focus on your existing clients and family.' She also shared her own past experience of turning things around after having a deal stolen from her at work. After listening, Yu Xiaowei's mood clearly improved. The two agreed that after the Guangzhou Marathon at the end of the month, Xiaowei would go to Shenzhen to have tea with Wenhui. The call lasted an hour.

events.name: After the call, record in diary and adjust mindset
events.description: After the video call ended, Yu Xiaowei sat alone in the living room for a moment, savoring Wenhui's encouragement. Then she took out her diary and wrote: 'Treat what is lost as a filter, and cherish what remains all the more.' She decided to stop meaningless anger and turn her focus back to work, family, and the marathon.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: When she got up, there was still a lingering feeling of gloom, but it was much better than last week.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Moved by friends' support, my inner conflict greatly decreased, and I felt recharged.

2025-10.daily_overview: On Wednesday, Yu Xiaowei's plans were interrupted by her daughter's high fever. She took leave from work and stayed home to take care of her daughter all day. In between, she studied CFP behavioral finance. During her lunch break, she had a video call with her coach Zhao Zhiming to adjust the training plan. In the evening, she shared stories of the Kowloon Walled City with her son, witnessed Lin Jiaxin's subtle emotional shift after independently getting her license, and once again reflected on possessiveness. At night, she did a video stretching session to maintain her training rhythm.

events.name: Daughter had a high fever; Yu Xiaowei took leave to care for her at home.
events.description: At 7 a.m., daughter Zhang Yuxin woke up with a burning forehead and a temperature of 38.8°C. Yu Xiaowei immediately called the company to ask for leave and was granted approval after explaining the situation. She measured her daughter's temperature, wiped her body with warm water to bring down the fever, and gave her children's fever-reducing medicine. She then called Teacher Wang, who was in charge of the ballet performance at the community center, to let her know that her daughter had a high fever and could not attend the rehearsal that day, and that the next step would depend on how she recovered. Her husband, Zhang Weiming, left work earlier than usual to help take care of their daughter.

events.name: Studying CFP behavioral finance in the gaps between caring for her daughter
events.description: At 10 a.m. and 3 p.m., while her daughter is asleep, Yu Xiaowei reads the behavioral finance chapter of the CFP course on her phone in the living room. She learns key investment biases such as overconfidence, confirmation bias, loss aversion, and completes 3 related practice questions. She briefly notes the key concepts in her notebook.

events.name: Video call with coach Zhao Zhiming during lunch break to adjust training
events.description: At 1 p.m., taking advantage of her daughter's nap, Yu Xiaowei contacted her coach Zhao Zhiming via WhatsApp video and reported on her training execution and diet control over the past 10 days. She said her legs felt heavy during running and her pace had dropped. The coach analyzed that it might be a normal reaction during the tapering period and suggested changing the planned 10 km easy run this weekend to 6 km and increasing the frequency of foam roller use. After the 15-minute call, she adjusted her training memo.

events.name: After dinner, shared podcast content with her son
events.description: Around 7 p.m. after dinner, Yu Xiaowei chatted with her 8-year-old son Zhang Zixuan on the sofa in the living room. She shared interesting stories about the history of the Kowloon Walled City she had heard on a podcast, such as its density and its self-governing order under anarchy. Her son was very excited and kept asking for more details. She promised to find an opportunity to take him to the Kowloon Walled City Park in the future.

events.name: Seeing that Lin Jiaxin had passed the exam, she reflected on her possessiveness.
events.description: At 8 p.m., in the WhatsApp best friends group, Yu Xiaowei saw Lin Jiaxin post her score report for the insurance intermediary qualification exam with the caption "I did it on my own." She was taken aback for a moment and wanted to send a private message to congratulate her, but seeing that it had already been posted publicly in the group, she simply gave it a like, while a sense of loss rose in her heart. She then reflected inwardly: "This is my possessiveness at work; it's a good thing Jiaxin is becoming independent." She realized that the friendship between the two was shifting from clinginess to a more mature, respectful adult relationship.

events.name: Evening video stretching session and core exercises.
events.description: At 9 pm, Yu Xiaowei had a video call with Shen Peiwen and did 30 minutes of dynamic stretching and core exercises. She did Cat-Cow, plank variations, and more, and shared her worries about her mindset before the full marathon. Shen Peiwen encouraged her to trust her training and handle it with a relaxed attitude. Afterward, she did 15 minutes of bedtime meditation and wrote in her gratitude journal, recording positive things such as her daughter's condition stabilizing and her friends' support.

events.name: Evening: recording her daughter's condition and medication
events.description: At 9 p.m. before bed, Yu Xiaowei recorded her daughter's three temperature readings that day (highest 39.1°C) and medication details in her phone memo, planning to decide the next day whether to take her to the doctor. She measured her daughter's temperature one last time—37.8°C, which had dropped somewhat—and felt a little reassured.

start_state.location: Bedroom at home.
start_state.mood: Woke up early, worried because her daughter had a fever, and quickly switched into caregiving mode.

end_state.location: Bedroom at home.
end_state.mood: Relieved that her daughter's condition was stabilizing, but felt a little complicated about Lin Jiaxin's independence. Overall tired, but after the training session and conversation, her mindset was a bit better.

state.daily_exercise: Evening video stretching session and core training, 30 minutes.

2025-10.daily_overview: Her daughter's high fever had subsided, but she still needed to rest. Yu Xiaowei communicated with the community center teacher about giving up the lead-dancer role, then comforted her daughter. She used her commute and lunch break to study behavioral finance cases, laying the groundwork for the CFP exam. Although she suspended her morning runs, she still stuck to meditation and eye yoga before bed.

events.name: Talked about giving up the lead dance role and comforted her daughter.
events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowei called the community center teacher to formally confirm that her daughter Zhang Yuxin could not serve as the lead dancer for the ballet performance because she had not recovered from a high fever. The teacher expressed understanding and arranged a replacement. Afterwards, beside her daughter's bed, she gently told her that although she couldn't dance lead on stage, she could watch her friends perform from the wings. Her daughter nodded obediently, and Yu Xiaowei felt both heartache and deep emotion.

events.name: Brief morning stretching.
events.description: Because her daughter was sick and she got up several times during the night to take care of her, she skipped her regular morning run and only did a 5-minute neck and shoulder stretch at home to relieve the exhaustion from the sleepless night.

events.name: Commute study: behavioral finance
events.description: On her way to work for the morning shift, Yu Xiaowei listened to a behavioral finance audio course on the subway, focusing on the impact of loss aversion and anchoring effects on real investment decisions.

events.name: Lunchtime eye yoga and case analysis
events.description: During her lunch break, she first did a five-minute eye yoga exercise, then used her laptop in the company conference room to simulate and analyze behavioral finance cases, marking difficult points she didn't fully understand and setting them aside for weekend review.

events.name: Evening family conversation and meditation
events.description: In the evening, her mother Chen Meiling specially made lung-nourishing soup for her granddaughter. Yu Xiaowei discussed her daughter's recovery and the weekend performance arrangements with her husband Zhang Weiming, and they decided the whole family would support their daughter. Before bed, she did 15 minutes of mindfulness meditation, wrote a short gratitude journal entry, and recorded her daughter's resilience.

In the afternoon, she focused on the CFP tax module in her home study and found time to embroider, completing part of the pattern for Daughter's World · Autumn.

events.name: Morning yoga stretching

events.name: Accompany daughter to the performance

Wearing a pretty little dress, Yuxin sat quietly in the wings watching her peers perform. Yu Xiaowei stayed with her throughout, gently comforting her from time to time.

events.name: Daughter's heartwarming words
events.description: After the performance ended, Yu Xiaowei hugged her daughter tightly, her heart full of guilt. But her daughter looked up and said, 'Mom, it's enough that dancing makes me happy.' Yu Xiaowei's eyes instantly welled up with tears, and the long-standing fatigue and anxiety were healed by her daughter's innocent words.

events.name: Studied the CFP tax module and Cantonese embroidery

events.description: In the evening, she watched an animated movie at home with her husband and children, enjoying family time. Before bed, she did meditation and eye yoga.

2025-10.daily_overview: The whole family cycled from Tai Wai to Tai Mei Tuk for a picnic, enjoying autumn family time; in the evening, a family meeting was held to decide on quarterly outdoor activities; at night, Yu Xiaowei focused on reviewing CFP mistakes and did post-competition mental rehearsal meditation.

events.name: Preparing for a picnic and cycling.
events.description: At 6 a.m., Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming made ham and cheese sandwiches and egg sandwiches in the kitchen, washed fruit and put it in insulated bags, and checked the cycling gear to make sure the child seats and first-aid kit were in good condition. At 7:30 they woke the children for breakfast, and at 8:00 set off for Tai Wai.

events.name: Family cycling at Tai Mei Tuk
events.description: At 9 a.m., the family arrived at the bicycle rental shop at the entrance of the Tai Wai cycling track. Yu Xiaowei and Zhang Weiming each rented a mountain bike and had a child seat installed on the back. Their son Zhang Zixuan took the lead on a children's mountain bike. They rode along the Tolo Harbour scenic route for about 3 hours. Throughout the ride, Yu Xiaowei controlled the pace, and Zhang Weiming followed closely with their daughter on board.

events.name: Picnic at Plover Cove Lake
events.description: At noon, they arrived at the shore of Plover Cove Reservoir in Tai Mei Tuk. The family chose a grassy spot under the shade of a tree, spread out a picnic mat, and enjoyed homemade sandwiches and fruit. As the autumn breeze blew, Yu Xiaowei and her husband admired the lake and mountain scenery while the children chased each other and played. She felt an unprecedented sense of relaxation in both body and mind.

events.name: Return bike ride
events.description: At 2 p.m., packed up, and the family cycled back to Tai Wai the same way. The return speed slowed down, and Yu Xiaowei kept paying attention to the children's stamina to ensure safety. At 4 p.m., returned to the rental shop and returned the bicycles, completing the full ride.

events.name: Family summary meeting
events.description: Returning home in the evening, Yu Xiaowei gathered her family in the living room for a brief review meeting. She proposed making family outdoor activities a quarterly tradition, and her husband and children agreed. Everyone discussed the next activity, and Yu Xiaowei recorded the plan in her phone's memo app, planning to implement it in January next year.

events.name: Evening review of CFP mistakes and pre-competition meditation
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei spent one hour intensely reviewing the wrong questions she had marked in this week's CFP study, and chose 10 comprehensive practice questions to complete within a time limit. Afterward, she did a 15-minute pre-race mental rehearsal meditation, imagining a smooth finish in the full marathon.

2025-10.daily_overview: On a workday, Yu Xiaowei sorted out the policy documents for her client Mrs. Chan in the morning, and went to Taikoo Shing in the afternoon for an annual review and to close a policy, receiving a referral; her family noticed her poor appetite, so her mother and husband adjusted dinner and comforted her through conversation; in the evening she resumed core strength training.

events.name: Organize Mrs. Chan's insurance policy documents
events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowei was in her study at home in Kowloon City District organizing the annual review materials for long-time client Mrs. Chen (Chen Meiling)'s family insurance policies, including the policy list, premium payment records, and changes in coverage amounts.

events.name: Go to Taikoo Shing for the annual review and sign the policy
events.description: In the afternoon, Yu Xiaowei set off from her home in Kowloon with documents, took the MTR to Mrs. Chen's home in Taikoo Shing, Eastern District, Hong Kong Island, to conduct a comprehensive annual review of the family insurance policies. She analyzed the existing coverage in detail and learned about changes and needs in Mrs. Chen's family recently. Based on Mrs. Chen's conservative wealth-management needs, she recommended a savings-type insurance plan bundled with medical insurance. After consideration, Mrs. Chen agreed and filled out the application form on the spot. Yu Xiaowei assisted in completing the signing process and explained the terms.

events.name: Received a referral
events.description: After the contract was signed, Mrs. Chen was very satisfied with Yu Xiaowei's professional service. Her father's tone was softer than before, and they agreed to go hiking together on the Double Ninth Festival. 2025-10.daily_overview: For her first full marathon—the Hong Kong Streetathon—Yu Xiaowei overcame cramps to finish with difficulty, with her family waiting at the finish line offering tremendous support; after the race she posted her reflections, and family bonds were strengthened.

events.name: Departing in the early morning for the starting point.
events.description: Woke up at 4 a.m., washed up, changed into running clothes, and checked the race bib, running shoes, and energy gels. Did 15 minutes of dynamic stretching in the living room and ate a banana. Left home at 5 and took a taxi to the Western Harbour Crossing Kowloon Toll Plaza starting point.

events.name: Full marathon race process
events.description: At 5:30 she arrived at the starting point and exchanged encouragement with fellow runner Shen Peiwen. The race started at 6:00 with the gun, and she moved steadily at a 6:10/km pace, passing the Western Harbour Crossing and the Central waterfront. She felt good passing the halfway point at 8:45. After 25 km she entered Sham Shui Po, and at 30 km her right hamstring suddenly cramped, forcing her to stop and walk. She took electrolytes and stretched, but the cramping kept recurring, so she could only alternate between running and walking. Relying on sheer willpower, she crossed the finish line at Victoria Park at 11:28 with a time of 5 hours 28 minutes, completing the full marathon of the Hong Kong Streetathon. She received the finisher's medal and was helped by volunteers to the recovery area.

events.name: Family members waiting at the finish line.
events.description: At 11:40, Yu Xiaowei met her waiting husband Zhang Weiming, son, and daughter in the rest area. Zhang Weiming handed her water and a towel; her son waved a small flag and cheered; her daughter hugged her tightly and said, 'Mom is amazing.' The family took a photo at the finish line, and Zhang Weiming had also prepared pineapple buns and milk tea.

events.name: Return home to rest and share after the race.
events.description: She returned home at 2 p.m., took a cold shower, did some simple stretching, and ate the wonton noodles prepared by her mother to replenish her energy. At 8 p.m., she posted her first marathon experience in the Hong Kong street marathon running group: "A full marathon is like life—you only know you can hold on after you break down." She attached a photo of herself crossing the finish line. The group responded enthusiastically. Shen Peiwen shared a photo of the two of them running together and replied, "Let's keep it up at the Standard Chartered race in December!" She was asleep before 22:00.

start_state.location: At home
start_state.mood: Excited

end_state.location: At home
end_state.mood: Extremely proud but physically exhausted

2025-10.daily_overview: On the Double Ninth Festival, Yu Xiaowei organized the whole family to climb Victoria Peak. During the climb, her father rarely showed concern about her work. At the summit, her father unexpectedly expressed trust in her, and the father-daughter relationship thawed. That evening, a warm family dinner was held, and for the first time her father asked Yu Xiaowei to help plan the estate.

events.name: Prepare hiking supplies
events.description: On the morning of the Double Ninth Festival, Yu Xiaowei prepared drinking water, snacks, and sunscreen for the mountain hike, reminded her father to bring his hiking pole, and her mother to prepare a jacket for the child.

events.name: The whole family sets off to climb Victoria Peak.
events.description: The family of six set off from their home in Kowloon City by private car, heading to the start of Lugard Road. Along the way, their father took the initiative to chat with the grandchildren, and the family atmosphere was harmonious. Yu Xiaowei felt gratified.

events.name: Brought up the topic of investing during the mountain hike
events.description: During the hike, Yu Xiaowei cautiously brought up the family investment and financial planning suggestion again. Her father was silent for a moment and did not respond. She felt slightly disappointed but did not press further. When they stopped to rest at the halfway pavilion, her father suddenly pointed to the financial tower in the distance and said, 'You work in that building—that's a lot of pressure, isn't it?' This was the first time in many years that he had asked about her work.

events.name: Unexpected reconciliation with her father after reaching the summit.
events.description: After reaching the summit of Victoria Peak, Yu Xiaowei took photos for everyone. When her husband was photographing her father, her father suddenly turned around and said, 'I'm old. I want to leave the money to you, but I don't trust those products. What I trust is you, Xiaowei.' Yu Xiaowei's eyes instantly became moist, and she hugged her father emotionally. Holding him, she felt that his shoulders were much thinner than in her memory. Her mother and the children also gathered around; it was a touching scene.

events.name: Playing at the hilltop and going down the mountain
events.description: After the whole family stayed at The Peak for about an hour, they came down along Mount Austin Road. On the way back, her father chatted happily with Yu Xiaowei, proactively asking about her work and letting her take some product materials home to look at.

events.name: Double Ninth Festival family dinner and preliminary communication on estate planning
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei cooked and prepared a family dinner herself. During the meal, she offered her father tea as a toast, thanking him for his trust. After dinner, the two talked privately in the living room. Her father explained his asset situation and inheritance ideas, hoping she would help develop a sound plan. Yu Xiaowei listened carefully and promised to handle it with care.

start_state.location: At home
start_state.mood: Expectant and nervous

end_state.location: At home
end_state.mood: Moved and relieved

2025-11.daily_overview: All day Saturday she stayed home studying for the CFP Investment Planning module—the last module in her CFP series certification. She had passed the foundation module in June; passing this module would complete the whole certification. In the early morning, after assessing her physical condition, she decided to go back to a regular breakfast to support her half-marathon training. During her lunch break, she designed a new diet and replenishment plan. In the afternoon, she found time to shop for ingredients. In the evening, she checked the bookkeeping app with her husband. She spent the entire day reviewing steadily in a final sprint.

events.name: Morning yoga and breathing exercises
events.description: Woke up at 6:15 in the morning and completed 15 minutes of yoga stretching in the Cantonese embroidery yoga space she had converted at home, accompanied by meditation music, but felt low on energy. Considering the high-intensity demands of the half marathon training plan, she realized that intermittent fasting was no longer suitable for her current stage, so she decided to end her 5-month 16:8 fasting and resume a regular breakfast from today.

events.name: Develop a nutrition and supplement plan for the training period
events.description: During a break in her morning review, Yu Xiaowei sat in the study during her lunch break and, based on her nutrition knowledge, designed a new breakfast menu — oatmeal porridge with eggs and banana, a pre-workout supplement of whole wheat bread and half a banana, and a post-workout supplement of protein powder shake. She then recorded the whole plan in detail in her phone memo.

events.name: Go to the supermarket to buy fresh ingredients
events.description: At 4 p.m., she took advantage of a dip in study efficiency and walked to the Wellcome supermarket near Prince Edward Road West. Following her memo, she bought whole-wheat bread, oats, eggs, bananas, and protein powder, stocking up on ingredients for the new diet plan starting the next day.

events.name: Final sprint before the CFP exam
events.description: She spent the whole day immersed in her study, focusing on reviewing the key formulas for investment planning and high-frequency behavioral finance cases, and redoing the set of incorrect questions from previous mock exams. While reviewing the key formulas, she recalled how unfamiliar she had felt when preparing for the basic module half a year ago; now she could grasp and connect them thoroughly, which gave her more confidence. At 10 p.m., she put away her materials and neatly placed her exam ID, calculator, and stationery into a document folder.

events.description: After dinner, she pulled her husband Zhang Weiming to open the expense-tracking app on their phones together, reviewed the overspending issues revealed in the October financial review, confirmed that this month's dining-out budget had been cut by 20%, and agreed that they would each insist on recording every expense with the app. They then updated the November family budget entries.

2025-11.daily_overview: On Monday morning, she learned that she had passed the CFP exam, but due to recent family and work troubles she had no interest in celebrating. She quietly filed away the materials and went to the company to handle client matters. In the afternoon, an old client politely declined to renew her insurance on short notice, leaving her downcast for a short while. In the evening, she happened to find a blank notebook and started the ritual of a gratitude diary, and proactively video-called her close friend Huang Wenhui in Shenzhen to clear up the doubts from her birthday. Her mood gradually warmed.

But thinking of how clients had recently been taken by competitors and her father's investment deadlock remained unresolved, she felt no joy. Carrying energy gels and electrolyte drinks, she put on her running shoes and race bib, set out from her home on Prince Edward Road West in Kowloon City, walked to Prince Edward MTR Station, and took the Tsuen Wan Line to the half marathon starting point in Tsim Sha Tsui.

events.name: Set a new personal best in the half marathon
events.description: At exactly 8:00 a.m., Yu Xiaowei started from the Tsim Sha Tsui Cultural Centre Piazza and followed the course through the West Kowloon Corridor, Mong Kok, and Sham Shui Po before returning to Tsim Sha Tsui. She maintained a steady pace of about 5 minutes 28 seconds per kilometer throughout, took an energy gel at the 10 km mark, and drank small amounts of water multiple times at water stations as planned. She finally crossed the finish line in 1 hour 55 minutes, trimming nearly two minutes off her personal half-marathon best, demonstrating excellent race strategy and physical fitness.

events.name: Post-competition systematic recovery
events.description: After crossing the finish line, Yu Xiaowei collected her finisher medal and a supply pack containing bananas, energy bars, and other items, then did about 15 minutes of static stretching in the recovery area, focusing on relaxing her quadriceps, hamstrings, and hip flexors. She took out the ice packs she had prepared in advance and applied cold compresses to both knees and ankles for about 10 minutes, and quickly drank the electrolyte drink she had brought and ate a protein bar to quickly replenish carbohydrates and repair muscles. While stretching, she vaguely felt that her eyes were a bit dry, and her vision was slightly blurry when she stared at the crowd in the distance, but she attributed it to the sea breeze and early-morning fatigue and did not pay much attention.

events.name: Won a fitness band in a lucky draw.
events.description: At the finish area, Yu Xiaowei saw that the sponsor Huawei's booth was holding a lucky draw, with prizes including fitness bands, running shoes, and more. She queued up to try her luck, not expecting that the on-site staff would announce that she had won a Huawei Band 8 fitness band worth 1,000 yuan. Excitedly, she took the prize from the staff, opened it on the spot, and wore it on her left wrist. For the first time, she was able to view her heart rate and cadence data in real time on the band's display, and she found it very novel and practical.

events.name: Warm family welcome at the finish line.
events.description: After recovering, Yu Xiaowei walked to the finish-line meeting area, where her husband Zhang Weiming was already waiting and handed her freshly brewed pour-over coffee he had made himself and kept in a thermos. Her son Zhang Zixuan and daughter Zhang Yuxin ran up excitedly and gave her hand-drawn colored cards, one depicting their mother's vigorous running posture and the other a family portrait, with wobbly handwriting reading 'Mom is the best.' The family hugged tightly. Her husband took a photo of Yu Xiaowei holding her medal and coffee, surrounded by the children. This warm moment made her deeply feel the power of family.

events.name: Return home to research the fitness band and continuation of eye-care habits.
events.description: Back home in Kowloon City in the afternoon, after showering and changing into loungewear, Yu Xiaowei sat on the living room sofa and carefully studied the various functions of the Huawei Band 8, including exercise modes, heart rate monitoring, sleep analysis, and blood oxygen detection. She decided to use the band for daily running training and nighttime sleep tracking, and planned to sync it with the Huawei Health App on her phone to record health data over the long term. At the same time, she continued to strictly follow her usual eye-care routine: turning on the eye-protection desk lamp in the study, using reading mode on her phone, and every 30 minutes of work or reading, looking into the distance at the green plants outside the window and doing a brief eye yoga session—moving her eyes up, down, left, and right—to reduce eye strain. After doing eye yoga once, she felt much relieved, but she had a faint sense that she had been spending too much time on screens recently and occasionally experienced blurred vision, so she silently noted to pay more attention.

events.name: Evening recovery and nutritional replenishment
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei felt some muscle soreness. She first took a warm shower to relax further, then changed into loose pajamas and lay down to rest. For dinner she ate the lean pork porridge and vegetable salad prepared by her mother Chen Meiling, and continued to hydrate. Around 8 p.m., she took out a foam roller and gave her thighs, calves, and back a light self-massage to relieve delayed-onset muscle soreness. She then went to bed at 21:50, did 5 minutes of mindfulness meditation before sleep, and wrote in her gratitude journal: “Today, I broke my half-marathon record, received the love of my family, and saw the meaning of my persistence.”

2025-11.daily_overview: Today was the first workday after the half marathon. Yu Xiaowei's body was still a bit sore, but she insisted on commuting to work. In the evening, she wrote in her diary to express her concerns about her recent vision decline and decided to give her fitness tracker to her husband Zhang Weiming, encouraging him to use data to pay attention to his health.

events.name: Morning commute and sense of physical recovery.
events.description: At 7 a.m., when Yu Xiaowei got up, she still felt delayed-onset muscle soreness in her thighs and calves. She did 5 minutes of simple morning stretching, then ate the oatmeal and scrambled eggs her mother had prepared. The scale showed 53.8 kg, slightly higher than yesterday; she knew it was water retention caused by muscle inflammation. She changed into a light gray suit dress, picked up her laptop bag, and took the MTR from Prince Edward Station to Wan Chai, a commute of about 55 minutes. At her desk, she placed a cushion to support her lower back and moved a little more slowly than usual, but she felt okay. During her lunch break, she did an eye yoga exercise as required to relieve screen fatigue.

events.name: On workdays, handle client insurance policies and team follow-up.
events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowei sat at her desk on the 12th floor of the AIA Building in Wan Chai, opened the CRM system to check the list of customers who needed policy renewals and expiration reminders within the past week, called three customers to confirm their renewals, and replied to several customer inquiry emails. In the afternoon, she briefly attended the team weekly meeting, where she updated the newcomer He Junwen and colleague Su Lishan on her recent half-marathon results and reminded everyone to pay attention to the insurance policy volume for the year-end performance push. The task list system continued to be implemented.

events.name: Wrote in her journal to express her anxiety about her eyesight.
events.description: After returning home from work in the evening, Yu Xiaowei opened her gratitude journal at the desk in her bedroom, but first wrote down her worries about her declining eyesight. She described in detail how prolonged use of phone and computer screens had caused dry, sore eyes, as well as occasional blurred vision after marathon training. She reflected that training fatigue and lack of nighttime sleep might have exacerbated the symptoms, and wrote down plans such as 'use the phone less' and 'keep doing eye exercises.' After writing for about 20 minutes, she felt some emotional release. She then did a 5-minute meditation to relax.

events.name: Gave the fitness tracker to her husband
events.description: After finishing her diary, Yu Xiaowei took her Huawei Band 8 to the living room and said to her husband Zhang Weiming: "I tried this band last night, and the sleep monitoring and heart rate data are really good. But I already have a sports watch for running, so the band is more suitable for you to wear every day—you're always climbing up and down repairing air conditioners, and you don't really pay attention to your heart rate and daily routine." She demonstrated the band's exercise, sleep, and heart rate functions to her husband and encouraged him to wear it. Zhang Weiming initially declined, but seeing his wife was sincere, he happily accepted and tried it on. The two immediately synced the mobile app and decided to manage their family health data together. She felt a little reluctant to give it up, but watching her husband curiously browse the functions after putting it on, she felt it was more valuable than staying in her drawer.

2025-11.daily_overview: Today Yu Xiaowei's schedule was especially packed: in the early morning she attended a restorative yoga class, in the morning she prepared materials for her performance review, in the afternoon she had her monthly performance discussion with her supervisor Liang Zhenhua, and in the evening she faced a sudden family financial worry—learning that her father had suffered investment losses privately. Amid mixed emotions, she stayed rational and discussed countermeasures with her husband.

events.name: Morning restorative yoga class
events.description: Because she had made an online reservation the previous night, Yu Xiaowei got up at 6 a.m., washed up, and weighed herself at 53.7 kg, slightly lower than yesterday. She put on yoga clothes, brought her yoga mat and towel, and walked seven minutes to the "Jingyue Yoga Studio" near her home for a 60-minute restorative yoga class focused on leg stretches, hip opening, and shoulder and neck relaxation, combined with abdominal breathing. During class, she felt her stiff muscles gradually loosen, and the teacher's gentle verbal guidance calmed her mind as well.

events.name: After yoga, decided to include it in the weekly training routine.
events.description: After the class, Yu Xiaowei talked with the yoga teacher about how her body felt after the half marathon. The teacher advised her to maintain one or two restorative sessions per week. On the walk home, she decided to make yoga a regular part of her training and set reminders in her phone calendar for Tuesday and Thursday mornings, and planned to bring Su Lishan along next time.

events.name: Morning: organizing sales data and preparing performance reviews.
events.description: At 9 a.m., Yu Xiaowei changed into professional attire and arrived at her desk in Wan Chai. She organized recent individual and team sales data into Excel charts, highlighting the conversion rate of high-net-worth clients and the progress of expanding the Shenzhen market. She reviewed the client follow-up issues raised at the last team review meeting and prepared a summary to report to Liang Zhenhua, including the personal brand effect brought by her impressive half-marathon result and the resources needed from her supervisor for Shenzhen market development.

events.name: Reserving a romantic dinner for the weekend
events.description: During lunch break, Yu Xiaowei remembered the planned dinner out with her husband on Saturday (the 22nd), so she called on her phone and booked a window seat for two at 18:30 that evening at Ice Room Time, a nostalgic Hong Kong-style Western restaurant in Mong Kok, and preselected the signature set meal for two and a bottle of mid-range red wine to prepare for the date.

events.name: Monthly performance review with supervisor Liang Zhenhua
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei went to Regional Sales Director Liang Zhenhua's office as scheduled for a one-on-one meeting. Liang Zhenhua first smiled and praised her excellent performance in the half marathon, then got down to business, pointing out that her recent pace of expanding local clients in Hong Kong had slowed, and suggested she strengthen referrals and penetration into community activities. Yu Xiaowei candidly shared the emotional ups and downs caused by her father's investment incident and the pressure from having clients taken away before. Liang Zhenhua expressed understanding, promised to coordinate marketing department resources to support her in developing the Shenzhen market, and encouraged her to turn pressure into motivation, setting a clear goal of adding at least 3 high-net-worth clients by December. The meeting lasted about 40 minutes, and both parties reached a consensus in a pragmatic atmosphere.

events.name: Evening: organized the meeting notes and action list.
events.description: Back home in the evening, Yu Xiaowei opened her laptop in the study and recorded one by one Liang Zhenhua's suggestions and his promised support. She listed a detailed action plan: a list of potential clients to call next week, specific steps to apply for resources to expand the Shenzhen market, and a plan to update WeChat marketing materials. After saving the file, she felt her direction was clearer.

events.name: Younger brother video-called to inform that father had investment losses.
events.description: At about 20:30, her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng sent a WeChat video call. He first congratulated his sister on her half-marathon result. When Yu Xiaowei asked about their father's recent investment moves, Yu Xiaofeng hesitated for a moment and then told her that their father, without telling them, had bought a non-principal-protected structured product through an old friend in the residential community. It had already lost about 30%, and the specific amount could be as much as HK$100,000. Yu Xiaowei was shocked and heavy-hearted. She realized that her father had made the decision on his own because he didn't want to trouble her, and she felt a mix of self-blame and worry.

events.name: Discussing countermeasures with my husband late at night
events.description: After hanging up the video call, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming closed the bedroom door and discussed the matter in detail. She recounted her father's situation in a low voice, her eyes slightly red, worrying about her father's retirement money and blaming herself for not helping him plan in time. Zhang Weiming held her hand and comforted her: 'We'll figure it out together.' The two agreed that Yu Xiaowei would arrange to talk to her father alone within the week, first to understand the details and calm him down, and then consider whether to use the family emergency fund to help him through this difficult time.

She was somewhat distracted at work during the day, but she still handled several urgent insurance policy matters. In the evening, she called her brother and gained a detailed understanding of the situation, preparing for a weekend meeting with her father.

events.name: Thoughts racing on the commute.
events.description: At 7:15 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei commuted to work by MTR as usual, but she kept silently looking out the window, replaying her younger brother’s words from last night in her mind. She mechanically transferred to Wan Chai Station and, before exiting the station, sent her husband a WeChat message: “I’ll ask Xiaofeng for the detailed information today—don’t worry.” Before leaving home, the scale had shown 53.6 kg, down another 0.1 kg from the previous day.

events.name: During work hours, handle policy renewals and client inquiries.
events.description: In the morning at her desk, Yu Xiaowei forced herself to concentrate. She completed online procedures for two medical insurance renewals and replied to a client's WeChat inquiry about the rate of return on an education fund insurance policy, sending the client screenshots of the specific figures. She also called her long-time client Chen Meiling to politely ask whether there had been any recent changes in her family finances, and made an appointment for a routine policy review next month. Although her efficiency was somewhat low, she basically completed the tasks that needed to be followed up that day. At noon, she did not forget to do eye yoga exercises to relieve dry eyes.

events.name: Called my younger brother to press for details about Father's investment
events.description: At 4:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowei left her desk early, walked to a quiet coffee shop near the office, and called her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng on her phone. In a calm but serious tone, she asked about the specific product name, purchase channel, amount invested, and extent of loss of her father's investment. Her brother told her that their father, on the recommendation of an old friend, had invested 100,000 Hong Kong dollars in a structured note product marketed by a private bank. It had lost about 30,000 so far, and because the product had a lock-up period, it was difficult to redeem immediately. Yu Xiaowei noted everything down in her phone memo and asked her brother to send photos of the product contract.

events.name: Go home and write in a journal to release emotions.
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei sat alone at the desk in her bedroom and opened her gratitude journal, but she wrote two full pages of worry and guilt about her father. She wrote: 'I thought giving him an allowance would be enough, but I forgot that he might need to feel needed more.' Tears quietly slipped down, but she also felt a sense of relief after writing. She then did 5 minutes of pre-sleep meditation and eye yoga, and lay down to rest at 21:30.

2025-11.daily_overview: Today Yu Xiaowei experienced two emotional shocks: her best friend Lin Jiaxin announced she would be joining a peer company as a competitor; after a brief stunned moment, Yu generously offered her blessings. At the same time, she gently invited her father to have tea over the weekend by phone, paving the way to resolve the investment crisis. In the evening, she did a mid-term review of her gratitude journal, which had been kept for several days, and felt that her insomnia was indeed improving.

events.name: Missed the early morning yoga class
events.description: This morning, Yu Xiaowei had accumulated fatigue from days of worrying about her father's investments. On top of that, the video from her younger brother the night before and the detailed loss figures lingered in her mind. Although she lay down at 21:30, she tossed and turned for nearly two hours before actually falling asleep, so she was only woken by the alarm clock at 6:45. She fretted in bed for a few minutes, but still got up to wash up. The scale showed 53.7 kg, a slight rebound. After some light stretching, she decided to postpone yoga and try to make it up tomorrow.

events.name: Received a long message from Lin Jiaxin and replied
events.description: At 8:20 a.m., while commuting on the subway, Yu Xiaowei saw a long message from her best friend Lin Jiaxin pop up in WeChat. Lin Jiaxin honestly told her that she would officially join a financial advisory company next month and might become a business rival in the future, but she still wanted Yu Xiaowei to be the first to know. After reading it, Yu Xiaowei was stunned for several minutes; it took the subway arrival announcement to snap her back to reality. Her feelings moved from surprise to relief. Thinking of how her friend, who had always relied on her, was finally becoming independent, she slowly typed out a reply with heartfelt pride: “I’m proud of you! Wherever we are, we’ll always be the best of friends.”

events.name: Daily work and team task follow-up
events.description: In the morning at her workstation, Yu Xiaowei opened her email and processed several reimbursement applications from team members. She also reviewed the client visit records of the new hire He Junwen and found signs of procrastination. She sent a message through the company's communication software reminding He Junwen that he must submit this week's visit summary the next day, and copied Liang Zhenhua. Afterwards, during her lunch break, she checked the family account balance on her mobile banking app, preparing herself mentally in advance for her father's investment rescue.

events.name: Calling Father to warmly invite him for weekend dim sum
events.description: At 3 p.m., Yu Xiaowei called her father from her office cubicle in a gentle voice: “Dad, it’s been a long time since we went to a tea house for dim sum. Are you free this Saturday afternoon? I’ll pick you up.” Her father, Yu Guoqiang, initially said there was no need to go to any trouble, but he gave in to his daughter’s insistence and finally agreed to meet at the usual place at two o’clock on Saturday afternoon. Yu Xiaowei didn’t mention the investment matter at all; she just wanted to see her father first.

events.name: Evening interim diary summary
events.description: After showering at night, Yu Xiaowei sat at the desk in her bedroom and looked through the gratitude diary she had started on November 3. She reviewed the little moments recorded over the past ten-plus days: guilt toward her father, workplace stress, anxiety about her eyesight, and small daily joys. She found that as she kept writing, her recent insomnia had clearly improved, the time it took to fall asleep shortened, and waking up startled from dreams also decreased. She wrote a resolution in her notebook: “I must keep writing; this is an inner space for myself.” After writing for about 20 minutes, she drew a small sun symbol beside the date with her fountain pen.

events.name: Briefly shared her feelings with her husband.
events.description: Before bed, Yu Xiaowei leaned against the headboard and said to her husband Zhang Weiming, who was taking off his fitness band: “Jiaxin is going to become a financial advisor. I feel a bit dazed, but more than anything, I'm happy. I'll talk about Dad's matter slowly on Saturday.” Zhang Weiming patted her on the shoulder and said, “Handle family matters one by one. You're doing great.” The two smiled at each other, turned off the light, and went to sleep.

At around 3:00, she saw Shen Peiwen, who had already arrived, at the entrance of the Tsim Sha Tsui section. The two waved and smiled, sizing up each other's running gear.

events.name: The last 10 km seaside jog
events.description: As usual, the two started running from the Tsim Sha Tsui section, jogging slowly eastward along the waterfront promenade toward Hung Hom at a relatively slow pace of 5 minutes 40 seconds per kilometer. They didn't talk much, only exchanging a few words occasionally, enjoying the harmony of running side by side. The sea breeze gently blew. When they reached the 5 km turnaround point, they stopped to drink some water. Yu Xiaowei said, 'We've run this route so many times.' Shen Peiwen nodded with a hint of melancholy. They easily completed 10 km within an hour, and finally walked slowly back to the bench near the starting point to rest.

events.name: Heartfelt goodbyes at sunset.
events.description: After the run, they sat on a bench, and the sunset dyed the sea orange and gold. Shen Peiwen spoke first: "Xiaowei, next month I'm going to Shanghai—a company transfer. From now on, I'll have to run alone." She shared her conflicting feelings about life in Hong Kong and Shanghai and her worries about family. Yu Xiaowei also revealed her unease: "Actually, I'm really afraid of being lonely. After you leave, I might have one fewer person to chat with all night." The two talked openly, both with moist eyes, but also felt the warmth of being trusted.

events.name: Giving a Cantonese embroidery lucky bracelet and agreeing to meet again.
events.description: Yu Xiaowei took a small silk pouch out of her backpack; inside was a deep blue bracelet she had embroidered herself, using Cantonese embroidery stitches to embroider the characters for 'peace' and two ginkgo leaves. 'I worked on this bracelet for several evenings. Wear it, and it's as if I'm walking with you.' Shen Peiwen took it in surprise and put it on immediately. They agreed to stay in touch via WeChat and solemnly promised to sign up for the Shanghai Marathon together next year and run side by side once more. Yu Xiaowei also took a selfie with Shen Peiwen on her phone, with the sunset glow in the background.

events.name: Returning home to reflect and share
events.description: After parting, Yu Xiaowei took a taxi alone back to Kowloon City. On the way, she watched the gradually brightening blue sky outside the window, feeling both warm and empty. After arriving home, she sent the group photo to the close friends chat with Lin Jiaxin and Huang Wenhui, briefly explained the reason, and also sent it to the running group. In the evening, she sat in the study, clipped a small bookmark Shen Peiwen had given her into her diary, and wrote today's gratitude entry: "Thank you, Shen Peiwen, for accompanying me all the way; friendship does not fade with distance." She meditated for 15 minutes before bed.

2025-11.daily_overview: Today, because her running friend Chen Zhiqiang took the initiative to buy insurance, Yu Xiaowei's professional conviction was deeply touched. She not only professionally configured insurance for Mr. Chen's whole family, but also reflected on her own professional attitude during the conversation. She was warmed by the words 'You just treat clients as people,' and gained a new understanding of the value of an insurance consultant. Morning yoga and evening fascia gun massage helped her body recover.

events.name: Morning yoga class
events.description: Got up at 6:00 in the morning, 53.3 kg. Went to the yoga studio for a class themed 'Hip Opening' to further relieve hip tightness after the half marathon. She felt her flexibility recovering.

events.name: Handle routine work and prepare for Mr. Chen's visit
events.description: In the morning at her workstation, Yu Xiaowei handled the verification of several automatically renewed insurance policies and spoke with Guo Junwei from the actuarial department by phone, asking about rate details for a few high-end medical products, to prepare for the afternoon meeting. She also deliberately changed into a smart dark blue suit, looking professional and approachable.

events.name: Running buddy Chen Zhiqiang visited to inquire about buying insurance
events.description: At 11 a.m., fellow runner Chen Zhiqiang arrived as promised on the 12th floor of the AIA Building. When Yu Xiaowei received him in the small meeting room, she silently marveled—this Mr. Chen was exactly the prospective client she had lost in April over quotation details, and in July he had filed fierce complaints about the sound of her nighttime running training footsteps downstairs. At first she had been turned away several times in the corridor, but later she kept proactively starting conversations and sincerely apologizing at running club activities, and the two gradually became running buddies instead. Mr. Chen said with a smile: 'I watched you cross the finish line at the previous half marathon. Your perseverance impressed me, so I feel you are trustworthy.' He expressed the wish to arrange a comprehensive and stable insurance plan for his whole family (himself, his wife, and his 8-year-old daughter).

events.name: Requirement analysis and recommendation of a conservative and steady plan
events.description: Yu Xiaowei asked Mr. Chan and his family about their ages, occupations, health conditions, and existing insurance coverage, and carefully recorded the details on her iPad. Then, based on their annual household income and assets, she recommended an insurance package: term life insurance of HK$1 million, critical illness insurance of HK$500,000 each, a high-limit medical supplement, and an endowment-style education fund policy. She explained the terms item by item, emphasizing in particular the certainty and long-term nature of the coverage, which matched Mr. Chan’s conservative preferences. Mr. Chan expressed satisfaction on the spot and was willing to proceed with underwriting. Mr. Chan nodded in approval and said with emotion, “Back when you ran in the middle of the night, I banged on your door to complain. I never thought I’d be sitting here now talking about insurance.” Yu Xiaowei smiled and replied, “It’s fate. Thank you for your trust all along.”

events.name: Over tea, she reflected on her professional beliefs
events.description: After signing the insurance application letter of intent, Yu Xiaowei chatted with Mr. Chen over instant black tea in the company pantry. Yu Xiaowei said with some emotion, 'I've been reflecting a lot lately. Am I too cautious with everyone? Could it make me seem cold?' Mr. Chen smiled and replied, 'You're not cold. You just treat clients as people, not as numbers. That kind of feeling is precious.' These words warmed Yu Xiaowei's heart, and she suddenly realized that her professional value lies in sincerely caring about others, which further strengthened her original resolve.

events.name: Evening fascia gun massage
events.description: Before bed, Yu Xiaowei carried out her Tuesday and Friday fascia gun massage plan, performing 20 minutes of self-massage on the front and back of her thighs and her back. Her muscles recovered well.

events.name: Share good news with her husband
events.description: In the evening, back at home, Yu Xiaowei mentioned to her husband at the dinner table how she had gained a new client's trust that day. Zhang Weiming was also pleased and casually said that his fitness band showed he had walked 13,000 steps today. Yu Xiaowei praised him for "making progress." After dinner, the couple watched an episode of a documentary about the preparation for the Shanghai Marathon and looked forward to their trip to Shanghai next year.

2025-11.daily_overview: Today Yu Xiaowei started preparing the legal work for her father's investment losses. She first consulted a legal advisor at the company, then took leave in the afternoon and went to her father's residence, talked with him in detail, and retrieved the complete contract documents. Although her father was resistant at first, he eventually handed everything over under her gentle insistence. In the evening, she went for a couples' night run with her husband to release stress.

events.name: Brief team task review in the morning
events.description: At the morning meeting, Yu Xiaowei spent only 15 minutes quickly following up on everyone's priorities for the day because she needed to leave early to handle family matters. She designated Su Lishan to temporarily act as the team contact for the afternoon, and then turned to her own tasks. Body weight: 53.2 kg.

events.name: Meeting with the company's legal counsel, Lawyer Chen.
events.description: At 10 a.m., Yu Xiaowei brought some contract photos provided by her father and found Lawyer Chen in the Legal and Compliance Department on the 11th floor of AIA Building. She briefly explained that the product her father bought was a non-principal-protected structured note, with a loss of about 30,000 yuan and an unexpired portion. After reviewing the terms, Lawyer Chen noted that although the contract included risk disclosure, the salesperson might have committed sales misrepresentation. To protect their rights, they would need to gather complete evidence, and he suggested starting with the bank's internal complaint channel. Yu Xiaowei took careful notes and agreed to contact him again if formal legal advice was needed later.

events.name: Took leave to go to her father's place to collect samples
events.description: In the afternoon, Yu Xiaowei left work two hours early after obtaining approval from her supervisor. She took the MTR to her father's residence in Kowloon City (not at the same place as her home; her father had another apartment). She brought a box of egg tarts that her father loved. At first her father avoided her gaze, but after she gently urged him, "Dad, I'm not blaming you. We want to help you minimize the losses," he finally took out all the remaining documents from the drawer: bank account statements, purchase receipts, risk disclosure forms, and so on. Yu Xiaowei photographed and backed up each one with her phone, comforted her father not to blame himself too much, and promised to first try communicating with the bank.

events.name: After returning home, the couple went for a night run.
events.description: That evening, Yu Xiaowei suggested going for a 5 km night run with her husband to clear their minds. The two jogged along Prince Road West at a pace of about 6:45 per kilometer, staying silent and running side by side. After the run, Yu Xiaowei felt much of the tightness in her chest had eased.

events.name: Organize materials and discuss
events.description: After the night run, Yu Xiaowei sorted and bagged the documents in her study and listed a timeline and key evidence points on the computer. Her husband Zhang Weiming made her a cup of chrysanthemum tea. The two discussed and, taking Lawyer Chen's advice into account, decided that she would first call the bank's customer service as a family member to request access to the sales process recording, while also evaluating the possibility of bearing part of the loss herself and switching to more prudent wealth management products.

For each category, she drafted different follow-up scripts and exclusive discount packages (such as first-year premium discounts or additional health services). She wrote the plan framework by hand on paper and decided to visit Shenzhen in mid-December in person.

Yu Xiaofeng readily agreed and said he could introduce her to a friend involved in the Shenzhen Insurance Technology Park project, who might be helpful for her cross-border business.

2025-11.daily_overview: The highlight of Saturday was reconciling with her father at a tea restaurant in the afternoon, where honest communication resolved the recent cold war and emotional knots. In the evening, Yu Xiaowei reviewed the family's November finances with her husband; because cutting back on eating out had worked well, savings rebounded, and they planned a Christmas gift budget, bringing the year to a steady close.

events.name: Relaxing family time in the early morning
events.description: She got up at 8 a.m., weighing 52.9 kg. Yu Xiaowei and her husband took their two children for a half-hour walk in the park downstairs, enjoying the fresh air. After returning home, she helped her mother air out the quilts. As the Cantonese proverb goes, 'Airing quilts is better than eating tonics.' The sun was shining brightly. She only did a simple morning stretch.

events.name: In the afternoon, met her father at a cha chaan teng to resolve the stalemate.
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowei arrived as planned at a long-established cha chaan teng in Kowloon City, where her father, Yu Guoqiang, was already seated in a booth. At first, they only exchanged pleasantries about family. After the milk tea and pineapple buns with butter were served, Yu Xiaowei gently brought up the investment. Her father finally let down his guard and admitted that, not wanting to trouble his daughter and having heard that an old friend had made money, he had bought in impulsively—never expecting to lose 30% of even the principal. His face was full of regret. Yu Xiaowei did not blame him. She simply reached across the table and took his hand: "Dad, money can be earned again. Don't be too hard on yourself. Weiming and I already have a plan to help you." She told him that she had filed a complaint with the bank and explained that she planned to use part of the family emergency fund to cover some of his losses and move the remaining funds into low-risk financial products. Her father's eyes welled up, and the impasse was finally broken. The two agreed to discuss the details of asset restructuring at home the next day.

events.name: Monthly family financial review.
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming sat in the study, opening the expense-tracking app and paper receipts. They checked November expenses item by item, including food, transportation, daily necessities, and the children's extracurricular classes, and found that dining-out costs had decreased by HK$820 compared with October, a significant improvement, with the monthly savings rate recovering to 85% of the target. The two were satisfied with the results. Next, they set a budget for Christmas gifts (500-800 Hong Kong dollars each for parents, mother-in-law, and each child), and planned to go shopping together next week. Given the recovery in savings, they agreed to add another HK$2,000 to the fixed deposit in December to get closer to the yearly goal of saving HK$50,000. Finally, they said goodnight to each other, feeling an added sense of teamwork from discussing finances together.

2025-11.daily_overview: Today, Yu Xiaowei had an in-depth asset restructuring discussion with her father. The father and daughter reached a sound plan that completely resolved the biggest source of recent distress. In the afternoon, she took the whole family to Tai Lam Country Park for a hike, enjoying quality outdoor time together. In the evening, she sorted through documents and reflected on this period of experience, feeling a heavier sense of family responsibility, but also more determined.

events.name: Early morning wake-up and preparation
events.description: At 6:10 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei was awakened by the vibration of her fitness band and weighed 52.7kg. She drank a glass of warm water and did 5 minutes of morning yoga stretching on the balcony with deep breathing. Then she polished the asset restructuring plan she had drafted and printed a clear table: Option 1 was to transfer the remaining funds into an AIA savings insurance product with guaranteed returns, held by her on his behalf; Option 2 was to convert them into a bank time deposit, with her adding a small monthly subsidy. She put the documents into a folder, ready to show her father.

events.name: One-on-one meeting with father about asset restructuring plan
events.description: At 10 a.m., Yu Xiaowei came to her father's room (after remarrying, her father still lived at another place nearby, but after yesterday's reconciliation, she came over specially this morning), and closed the door. She first calmed her father down, then laid out the plan: "Dad, here's what we'll do: I'll set aside 50,000 yuan from the family emergency fund to help you cover part of the principal loss. I'll move the rest of the money into a principal-protected wealth management plan, so it won't lose money again. From now on, I'll review all your investments before you decide." After hearing this, her father nodded silently, accepted the plan, and promised to discuss all future investments with his daughter first. Yu Xiaowei put away her father's written authorization and planned to go to the bank next week to handle it.

events.name: Afternoon family outdoor hike
events.description: In the afternoon, Yu Xiaowei suggested the whole family go hiking in Tai Lam Country Park to enjoy the warm winter sun. The couple, with their son and daughter and her mother-in-law Chen Meiling, drove toward Tuen Mun and walked along a section of the Family Trail beside Tai Lam Chung Reservoir for about 1.5 hours, covering about 6 kilometers in total. The children ran around in nature, and her mother-in-law walked slowly with her husband's support. Yu Xiaowei took a family photo with her phone and felt that this was the meaning of her hard work.

events.name: Evening: organizing materials and reflecting
events.description: After returning home in the evening, Yu Xiaowei reorganized her father's investment-related documents in the study and formally marked the item “Handling Father's Losses” in the family financial ledger. She took out her gratitude journal and wrote: “Today I helped Dad take the first step, and I feel the whole family is closer. The responsibility is heavy, but I can handle it.” Looking at the photos of her sleeping husband and children, she felt that the turmoil of the past half month was settling down and life was slowly returning to normal. Before bed, she did 15 minutes of meditation and turned off the lights at 22:50.
